articleTitle: High-Performance GaN HEMTs on Single Crystalline AlN Templates with a 230 nm Ultra-Thin Buffer and Al2O3/SiO2 Passivation
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: Single crystalline AIN templates are a promising candidate for fabricating <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\geq 1200$</tex> V low-cost and high-performance GaN power HEMTs, which feature a high crystal quality and an ultra-thin buffer. In this work, GaN HEMTs have been successfully fabricated and evaluated on the 2-inch 500 nm single crystalline AIN templates, which are made on sapphire substrates through 1700 °C annealing. HEMTs with a 230 nm ultra-thin buffer demonstrate a high blocking voltage over 2700 V with gate-drain spacing L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">GD</inf> of 22 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu\mathrm{m}$</tex>. Benefiting from the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Al}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3}/\text{SiO}_{2}$</tex> passivation, the fabricated HEMTs exhibit a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$< 15\%$</tex> dynamic R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ON</inf> degradation and a negligible threshold voltage V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TH</inf> shift. This work proves that GaN HEMTs on the single crystalline AlN templates are likely to play an important role for future <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\geq 1200\ \mathrm{V}$</tex> GaN products.

articleTitle: The Role of Line-Shaped Defects in Premature Breakdown of $\beta-\text{Ga}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3}$ Power Diode and Suppression by Oxygen Annealing
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: In this work, we illuminate the impact of line-shaped defects (LDs) on the premature breakdown phenomena observed in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta-\text{Ga}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3}$</tex> Schottky barrier diodes (SBDs). Adopting the Conductive Atomic Force Microscopy (C-AFM) and Kelvin Probe Force Microscopy (KPFM) technique, it has been determined that LDs manifest local electrical properties characterized by larger reverse current and lower surface potential. Additionally, the high-temperature oxygen annealing has been proved to be an effective method in decreasing this killer defect density, in favor of the fabrication of SBDs with a breakdown voltage in excess of 2100 V. This study establishes a relationship between the blocking ability of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta-\text{Ga}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3}$</tex> SBDs and killer defects, offering valuable insights into the mechanism underlying the reverse characteristics of SBDs, as well as guidance for high-quality crystal growth and device design.

articleTitle: 200mm GaN-on-Si E-Mode Power HEMTs with Epitaxially Grown p-AlN/p-GaN Gate to Enhance Gate Reliability
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: E-mode power HEMTs with epitaxially grown p-AlN/p-GaN gate are demonstrated for the first time to enhance the gate reliability, including the positive bias temperature instability (PBTI), time-dependent gate breakdown, and the high-temperature gate bias (HTGB). Furthermore, the electroluminescence (EL) emission is conducted to evaluate the electrons-holes recombination through the Magnesium acceptor and deep-level donor in the p-AlN layer, and the TCAD simulations indicate that the hole barrier tunneling can be reduced from the Schottky metal/p-AlN/p-GaN interfaces by using epitaxially grown p-AlN/p-GaN gate stack.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Study on Trapping-Induced Dynamics in β-Ga2O3Schottky Barrier Diodes Under Continuous Switching Stress
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive study of the static and dynamic characteristics of Schottky barrier diodes based on a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta$</tex>-phased gallium oxide <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\text{Ga}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3})$</tex>. The dynamic performances of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta-\text{Ga}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3}$</tex> SBDs under continuous switching stress show a significant Schottky barrier height instability. The barrier height increases along with the increase of negative stress voltage <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(V_{\text{stress}})$</tex>. An optimized current transient methodology for characterizing device trap information is proposed. The set of dominant trap active energy is characterized as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E_{\mathrm{c}}-0.76\ \text{eV}, -0.62$</tex> eV, and −0.47 eV. These findings provide evidence of possible instability of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta-\text{Ga}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3}$</tex> based devices in power switch applications and offer a path for reducing instability issues.

articleTitle: A Novel GaN Gate Driver: Transistor-Intrinsic Integration Exploiting Non-Ideal Characteristics by Device-Circuit Co-Design
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: This work introduces a device-circuit co-design strategy that can leverages non-ideal effects, including parasitic effects, to benefit integrated circuits (ICs), thereby substantially improving the integration level. An innovative transistor-intrinsic charge pump that eliminates the need for additional capacitor and diode is proposed. Based on the charge pump, a novel transistor-intrinsic gate driver with a compact topology, composed entirely of enhancement-mode HEMTs (E-HEMTs), has been realized using the commercialized technology of p-GaN gate HEMT. The gate driver, comprised solely of six E-HEMTs, achieves rail-to-rail output while maintaining low power consumption and thermal stability. Experimental results indicate that the proposed driver's dynamic output high level (VOH) is 2.36 V above its static counterpart and 1.36 V higher than the classic driver, thus achieving rail-to-rail output. From 25 to 200 °C, the load current degradation rate in this driver is merely half of that observed in conventional designs, ensuring driver's high-temperature stability. The results demonstrate the practicality of device-circuit co-design and transistor-intrinsic integration in compact all-GaN ICs, providing a new perspective for GaN integration technology.

articleTitle: Field Plate Engineering for Free Metal Routing over Lateral HV Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: This work reports on novel field plate structures, aimed at protecting large-area lateral HV devices from overlying metal layers. This gives freedom to IC design regarding metal routing on top of power devices and isolation structures in Power Integrated Circuits (PICs), in particular for voltages exceeding 150V. These field plates maintain or even enhance HV device characteristics. The method is applicable to any high voltage supporting lateral structure including drift regions and termination regions of lateral and even vertical HV devices.

articleTitle: High VTH and Breakdown Enhancement-Mode GaN HEMTs for Power ICs Application Using Charge Trapping Layer
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: This work demonstrates a high V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TH</inf> (+8.4 V) and breakdown voltage (1100 V) Enhancement-mode GaN HEMTs using an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Al:HfO}_{\mathrm{x}}$</tex>-based charge trapping layer (CTL). The operation mechanism is investigated through TCAD simulation, and the device performance is systematically evaluated through static and dynamic electrical measurements. Thanks to the V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TH</inf>is tunable by initialization voltage, we prove that the fabricated CTL-based GaN inverters can operate under a variety of conditions (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta=10-40$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{V}_{\text{DD}}=3$</tex> V-15 V) with commendable output swing and noise margins. These results present a promising approach towards to realizing the monolithic integration of GaN devices for power ICs applications.

articleTitle: Novel Grid-Gate 16V-nLDMOS with a Low Specific On-Resistance of 4.7mΩ.mm2Based on A Standard 0.18μm BCD Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: A novel 16V Lateral Double-diffused MOSFET (LDMOS) based on a standard 0.18 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mu\mathrm{m}$</tex> BCD platform is reported in this work, which uses grid-gate technology to realize the 35V off-state breakdown voltage <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\text{BV}_{\mathrm{O}\mathrm{F}\mathrm{F}})$</tex> with a reduction in the specific on-resistance <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{o}\mathrm{n},\mathrm{s}\mathrm{p}})$</tex> from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$6.8\mathrm{m}\Omega\cdot \text{mm}^{2}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$5.9\mathrm{m}\Omega\cdot \text{mm}^{2}$</tex>. By utilizing the single buffer structure and buffer RESURF composite structure, the proposed grid-gate 16V-nLDMOS is optimized to meet the requirements of 28V <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{BV}_{\mathrm{O}\mathrm{F}\mathrm{F}}$</tex> and the measured <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{R}_{\mathrm{o}\mathrm{n},\text{sp}}$</tex> is reduced to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$4.7\mathrm{m}\Omega\cdot \text{mm}^{2}$</tex>. What's more, TLP experiments on the samples illustrated that the proposed buffer structures can extend the safe operation area (SOA) of grid-gate LDMOS to satisfy the need for DC-DC application.

articleTitle: Highly Optimized High-Voltage SOI p-LDMOS Beating the Conventional SOI Limit
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: In this paper we demonstrate a novel STI based p-LDMOS that is shown to surpass the conventional SOI (Silicon-on-Insulator) BV (breakdown) limit. Based on TCAD simulations it is revealed that the ultimate breakdown is enhanced due to hole inversion along silicon/BOX (buried oxide) interface which pins the potential. This allows us to utilize the silicon epi thickness to drop the potential from source to drain. It also presents an interesting case to carefully design an optimal SOI architecture.

articleTitle: Vertical GaN Superjunction Diode on Sapphire with Kilovolt Dynamic Breakdown Voltage
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: The development of superjunction structures for use in vertical wide bandgap power devices promise to break the 1-D material limits. Additionally, the possibility of utilizing heteroepitaxial GaN-on-Sapphire wafer for vertical devices can significantly trim the material and device cost. This work introduces a quasi-vertical GaN-on-Sapphire superjunction PN diode design utilizing sputtered p-NiO on the etched GaN fins for superjunction formation. DC breakdown voltage is shown to vary with superjunction charge imbalance and significantly exceed the expected 1-D planar limit of 350V given the epilayer design used. A maximum breakdown voltage of 840 V is extracted for near charge balance conditions limited by leakage current. Dynamic breakdown of the device is characterized as a function of reverse voltage slew rate. A maximum dynamic breakdown voltage of 1160 V under a reverse voltage slew rate of 2000 V/μs is found.

articleTitle: Physics-based Compact Model for Multi-channel AlGaN/GaN Schottky Barrier Diodes
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: This paper showcases a simple yet comprehensive compact model for multichannel AlGaN/GaN Schottky-barrier diode (SBD) with a p-GaN RESURF layer. Model formulation, including equivalent circuit, key equations, and parameter assign-ment, are explained in details, together with parameter extraction flow. The model correctly reflects the device physics in forward-bias, reverse-bias and breakdown conditions, capturing critical behaviors associated with multi-channel turn-on and RESURF effects from the p-GaN layer. Good accuracy, scalability, and computation robustness are validated via: IV, CV, breakdown simulations. The physics-based model can also be used as a tool for technology optimization and scaling projections. This is illustrated via simulations on (1) the impact of barrier/channel thickness on device capacitance and (2) the effect of RESURF-length <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(L_{RE\mathrm{S}URF})$</tex> on the Baliga Figure-of-Merit (FoM) and area-scaling FoM. With minimum adjustment, the proposed model also serves as a first step towards compact modeling of multi-channel AlGaN/GaN transistor.

articleTitle: Monolithically Integrated >3kV, 20A 4H-SiC BiDFET Utilizing an Accumulation Mode Channel for Improved Output Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: This paper presents the first successfully demonstrated monolithically integrated <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$> 3\text{kV}$</tex> 4H-SiC Bi-Directional FETs (BiDFETs) fabricated utilizing both accumulation-mode and inversion-mode channels. BiDFETs demonstrated enhanced output characteristics in both the forward <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{S}1\rightarrow \mathrm{S}2)$</tex> and reverse <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{S}1\leftarrow \mathrm{S}2)$</tex> directions, by employing the higher channel mobility and channel diode component of the accumulation-mode channel. This lower knee voltage, in conjunction with a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{R}_{\text{on,sp}}$</tex> reduction for accumulation channels, led to a 9.6% reduction in overall <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{V}_{(\mathrm{S}2-\mathrm{S}1)}$</tex> at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{I}_{\mathrm{S}2-\mathrm{S}1)}=20\mathrm{A}$</tex>, while also mimicking the blocking capabilities of the inversion-mode channel.

articleTitle: Suppression of Hot-Electron-Induced Dynamic RON Degradation in p-GaN Gate HEMT Using Active Passivation and Virtual Body
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: The dynamic RON performance of GaN power devices is reported to degrade after hot-electron stress, due to the generation of new traps. In this study, the p-GaN gate HEMTs with active passivation and virtual body (AP/VB-HEMTs) are proposed to address hot-electron induced dynamic degradation. The active passivation is a thinned p-GaN layer that extends from the gate towards the drain. The virtual body is a hole channel above a buried AlGaN layer, and is formed by holes injected from gate. As a result, the surface trapping caused by pre-existing and hot-electron generated traps are screened by the active passivation. The buffer traps are suppressed by the mobile holes in virtual body. To evaluate the effectiveness on suppressing hot-electron induced dynamic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R_{\text{ON}}$</tex> degradation, the devices are evaluated after hot-electron stress with different stress time and stress current. After a 30-min hot-electron stress, the AP/VB-HEMT shows negligible dynamic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R_{\text{ON}}$</tex> increase, presenting a contrast to the severe degradation in conventional p-GaN gate HEMT, suggesting the enhanced suppressions against hot-electron stress in the AP/VB-HEMT.

articleTitle: CMOS Gate Driver with Integrated Gate Current Monitoring Method for Fault Under Load Short Circuit Detection of SiC Power Modules
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: Existing literature has primarily focused on using gate signals for short-circuit type I detection (Hard Switch Fault, HSF). However, an unaddressed aspect remains in detecting the short-circuit type II (Fault Under Load, FUL). This article introduces a Gate-Driver (GD) IC with a fully integrated approach for the FUL detection. This solution strategically uses the gate current copy, enabling ultra-fast FUL detection. Experimental results demonstrate reliable fast short-circuit detections for power modules, in less than 100ns. This IC is fabricated using NXP Semiconductors' high-voltage SMARTMOS10 130nm CMOS SOI technology.

articleTitle: 3D Simulation Study of a Novel 1200 V IGBT Concept for EMI-Critical Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: We present a novel 1200-V IGBT concept especially designed for switching with low electromagnetic interference (EMI) noise, as e.g. required for drives applications. These can suffer from EMI problems arising from diode snap-off oscillations at very low currents. A conventional solution would be to limit the dI/dt and dV/dt of the IGBT to exhibit less switching stress on the diode, which usually increases losses of the inverter at nominal conditions. The novel structure shows unique properties which lower switching and on-state losses at nominal conditions, while successfully reducing the switching slopes at very low currents resulting in improved performance.

articleTitle: In-Situ Extraction of Time-Resolved $E_{\text{OSS}}$ on GaN Power Device Based on a Modified Hard Switching Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C_{\text{OSS}}$</tex> loss (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E_{\text{OSS}}$</tex>) and Dynamic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R_{\text{ON}}$</tex>, which combine switching loss and conduction loss in currently available GaN HEMTs, severely limit their performance in hard switching topologies. The effect of dynamic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R_{\text{ON}}$</tex> under various stress conditions have been extensively explored. However, Coss discharge process remains elusive, as the current flowing through Coss cannot be detected directly. This work proposes an easy-to-implement method to extract the dynamic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E_{\text{OSS}}$</tex> under long-term OFF-state drain stress and hard-switching stress. The dynamic FOM <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R_{\text{ON}}\times E_{\text{OSS}}$</tex> dependence on the continuous hard-switching stress is investigated, which is critical for the insights into the physical origin of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C_{\text{OSS}}$</tex> loss and practical application.

articleTitle: 1.2 kV-Class Double Gate CSTBT™ with Carrier Profile Control for Total Switching Loss Reduction of Turn-Off and Tum-On
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: The 1.2 kV-class double gate carrier stored trench-gate bipolar transistor (DG CSTBT™) with carrier profile control is demonstrated to achieve a total reduction in switching losses of both turn-off and turn-on. To examine the effect of carrier profiles on DG CSTBT™., devices with the identical <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{\mathrm{C}\mathrm{E}(\mathrm{s}\mathrm{a}\mathrm{t})}$</tex> value but varying carrier profiles were fabricated by adjusting the doping concentrations of the p- collector and carrier stored layer. To comprehensively investigate the impact of DG driving on the switching characteristics., the trade-off relationships between switching losses and dV/dt are evaluated. Under a specific value of dV/dt., DG CSTBT™ with a low-doped p-collector and a high-doped CSL resulted in a 26% reduction in the total switching losses of turn-off and turn-on. Additionally, SCSOA and RBSOA were successfully maintained for DG CSTBT™ with carrier profile control.

articleTitle: Experimental Investigation of a Novel 750V SJ-RET-IGBTs (Superjunction Recessed Emitter Trench IGBTs) for the Automotive Application
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: The soaring demand for electric vehicles has made it evident that the Insulated Gate Bipolar Transistor (IGBT), a crucial component, needs to evolve. To minimize switching loss, we need to focus on optimizing the front-side design and enhancing the drift region. Introducing finely patterned super junctions to replace the flat concentration drift region allows us to take traditional IGBTs to new heights, and the results are remarkable. In this work, using 8-inch wafer mass fabrication with the fine pattern cell and super junction structure, we can enhance switching performance by up to 30% while keeping the equal conduction loss, maintaining high ruggedness, and a broad safe operating area.

articleTitle: A Discrete Channel Model to Estimate Threshold Voltage Deviation Induced by The Voltage Stress in SiC Short Channel MOSFETs
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: The threshold voltage <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(V_{TH})$</tex> of silicon carbide (SiC) MOSFETs are affected by the coupled effect including the SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/SiC poor interface and the short channel effects (SCEs), and this coupled effect is directly related to gate voltage <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(V_{GS})$</tex> and drain voltage <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(V_{DS})$</tex>. This paper introduces a discrete channel model to estimate the V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TH</inf> deviation caused by the different voltage stress on both sides of SiC MOSFET short channel. Transfer characteristics are used to verify the accuracy of the model. It is indicated that the poor interface is the dominant factor for these deviations of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{TH}$</tex>, Power MOSFETs were fabricated to further validate the model and revealed that the source resistance also contributes to the deviations especially with the increasing of drain-source current in MOSFET.

articleTitle: Individual Control of Paralleled SiC-MOSFETs with Nano-Second Level Switching Timing Synchronization
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: This paper describes a control method that feeds back the switching timing of SiC-MOSFETs connected in parallel to suppress switching current concentration. The voltage generated by the inductance of the source electrode during switching is detected by the detection circuit and used as a feedback signal. Compare the time difference of feedback signals for each SiC-MOSFET with 1nane-second (nsec) resolution using FPGA. Current concentration can be suppressed by adjusting the timing of the gate signals so that the time difference is minimized automatically. This control is also effective against changes in SiC-MOSFET characteristics over time, such as gate deterioration and increase in thermal resistance occurred by power cycles. The effectiveness of the developed control on gate degradation and increased thermal resistance is demonstrated through experiments.

articleTitle: Threshold voltage instability of p-GaN Gate HEMT in 48-12V Buck Converter & its Impact on Circuit Power Loss Variation
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: From the circuit perspective, the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{\text{th}}$</tex> instability during circuit operation and its impact on the circuit performance is studied based on a 48–12 V buck converter operates in hard-switching (HS) mode. Unexpectedly, even in the normal circuit operation condition, substantial <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta V_{\text{th}}=+0.2\sim + 0.83$</tex> V at varied frequency (<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f$</tex>) and output current <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(I_{\text{out}})$</tex> were measured in the p-GaN gate HEMTs and the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta V_{\text{th}}$</tex> exhibits a positive correlation with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I_{\text{out}}$</tex>. HS double-pulse test as well as on- and off-state stress tests on discrete devices reveal that the hard-switching transient-state is a critical factor causing <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{\text{th}}$</tex> instability, while the underlying mechanisms is analyzed in detail. In addition, the impact of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{\text{th}}$</tex> instability on the overall circuit power loss are quantitatively investigated. For instance, at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$f=1.9$</tex> MHz & <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I_{\text{out}}=2\ \mathrm{A}$</tex>, the deadtime power loss significantly increased by 35.35%. The overall power loss consumed by GaN HEMTs increased up to 11.6%.

articleTitle: Polarization-Assisted Acceptor Ionization in E-Mode GaN p-FET on 650-V E-mode p-GaN Gate HEMT (EPH) Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: There is a strong motivation to develop E-mode p-channel field-effect transistor (p-FET) on the E-mode p-GaN gate HEMT (EPH) platform to enable complementary logic (CL) circuits and power integrated circuits (PICs). However, the p-FET on such platform often presents a low current density (1-5 mA/mm). A major cause is the low ionization rate of acceptors in p-GaN. This work demonstrates a polarization engineering technique that aims to enhance the ionization of acceptors in p-GaN layer. By inserting a thin AlN layer (~1.5 nm) into the p-GaN, the polarization field of AlN pushes down the energy band of the lower p-GaN layer, leading to enhanced ionization of acceptors. The AlN layer also creates an energy well above AlN for holes, resulting in modulation doping effect and enhanced two-dimensional hole gas (2DHG) above AlN. The fabricated p-FET with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_{\mathrm{G}}=2$</tex> μm exhibits an E-mode operation with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{\text{th}}$</tex>= −0.8 V. A low RON of 1.1 kΩ.mm is obtained. The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I_{\text{ON}}/I_{\text{OFF}}$</tex> is over 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup>. The <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I_{\max}$</tex> is 10.8 mA/mm, which is among the largest values in literature for E-mode GaN p-FETs on the EPH platform. Finally, an E-mode n-channel p-GaN gate HEMT is demonstrated on the same epitaxial wafer, validating the capability of the platform for CL and PICs.

articleTitle: Temperature-Dependent Mechanism of Short-Circuit Voltage Imbalance in Series-Connected SiC MOSFETs
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: The series connection of SiC MOSFETs is a cost-effective solution to enable higher voltage applications. Nevertheless, proper voltage sharing remains challenging for reliable operation. This paper investigates the voltage imbalance issues during short-circuit stress. Experimental results show the unbalanced voltage of two devices even with similar characteristics. Since the imbalance issue is affected by swapping only the two gate drivers upside down, the intrinsic delay between gate drivers is regarded as an initial cause. The results from mixed-mode electro-thermal TCAD simulations indicate that the temperature-dependent mechanism plays a large role in the voltage imbalance.

articleTitle: Global Potential Control Technique Used in Isolation Structure for 1200V HVICs
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: The global potential control technique regards the potential distribution of each part in the 1200V isolation structure as interacting. The potential distribution of high voltage junction termination (HVJT) is extracted by the potential delivering field plates (PDFPs) with uniform arrangement, and a new potential distribution is formed with the change of PDFPs' spacing on the P-isolation ring region. When the PDFPs are extended to the P/N-channel lateral diffused metal-oxide-semiconductor (P/NLDMOS), the spacing is widened near the source/drain side and is narrowed on the middled drift region. The potential distributions of LDMOS are redistributed by the PDFPs, which suppresses the premature leakage effectively. The breakdown voltage (BV) of the isolation structure has a 364% improvement, even though the doping concentration of the P-drift is taken to a very high value.

articleTitle: A Fully Realised ‘Dielectric Field Relief’ TrenchMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: Nexperia has developed a low-cost novel device concept, with high avalanche ruggedness, low output charge (QOSS) and reduced on-state resistance (Rds(on)) for any given Vds rating. This exciting technology uses the principle of ‘Dielectric RESURF’ to achieve the required breakdown voltage by utilizing proprietary process techniques to grow an extended Thick Barrier Oxide (eTBO) throughout the active gate trench network, removing the requirement for a super junction or shield field plate to achieve the RESURF.

articleTitle: An Enhancement-Mode Algan/GaN HEMT with Island-Ohmic p-GaN Featuring Stable Threshold voltage and Large Gate Swing
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: A novel AlGaN/GaN HEMT based on an Island-Ohmic p-GaN gate (IO-PGaN) structure is proposed. Thanks to the Island-Ohmic, the “floating” p-GaN is connected with the gate terminal via the heavily doped p++-GaN island. Therefore, the net charges generated in the p-GaN region under the gate or drain stress conditions, could be easily compensated by supplying holes via the ohmic gate structure, resulting in a stable threshold voltage (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TH</inf>). Meanwhile, a SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> side wall is intentionally formed to achieve a moderate E-field at the island corner, and a JFET-like structure formed by the Schottky-metal/p-GaN junction delivers a self-limited gate leakage.

articleTitle: Gate Switching Instability of SiC MOSFETs under Simultaneously High Drain-Source Voltage and High Frequency Acceleration
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: SiC MOSFETs have recently been found to suffer from a prominent threshold voltage drift when applying an alter-nating voltage to the gate under certain conditions. In contrast to the well-known bias temperature instability (BTI), this newly observed degradation mechanism is dependent on the number of cy-cles performed and was termed gate switching instability (GSI). This paper presents the influence of an additional high electric field on gate reliability during GSI testing. Therefore, a new test concept is introduced where gate switching stress (GSS) is carried out, and simultaneously a high drain-source voltage is applied. The results of these frequency-accelerated tests on state-of-the-art SiC MOSFETs with different device technologies are shown and compared to non-high voltage GSS tests.

articleTitle: Self-Protection Mechanism of Schottky-Type p-GaN Gate HEMTs Under Forward Gate ESD Stress
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: The gate-side HBM (human body model) ESD robustness of Schottky-type p-GaN gate HEMTs is investigated. The maximum reverse gate current and gate breakdown voltage in the quasi-static I-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V$</tex> tests are higher than the forward cases, whereas the forward gate ESD robustness is much stronger than the reverse case. Such contradiction is caused by a self-protection mechanism under forward gate ESD stress. The capacitive division of the forward gate voltage in the two junctions of the p-GaN gate stack induces high transient electron thermionic emission current through the p-GaN/ AlGaN/GaN p-i-n junction. This current dominates the forward gate current and enables substantial charge leakage from the HBM capacitance. The self-protection mechanism analysis is facilitated by a custom-designed pulsed <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I$</tex>-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V$</tex> test system based on SiC MOSFETs, which can generate high current (up to 26 A) pulses with short pulse width <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\leq 90\ \text{ns})$</tex>.

articleTitle: Demonstration of Surface Treatment for $\beta-\text{Ga}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3}$ Schottky Barrier Diode with High Breakdown Voltage and Low Specific On-Resistance
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: In this work, the influence of different surface treatments on the breakdown voltage (BV) and the specific on-state resistance <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(R_{on,sp})$</tex> of the beta-phase gallium oxide <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\beta-\text{Ga}2\mathrm{O}_{3})$</tex> Schottky barrier diodes (SBD) is investigated. The results show that after fast inductively coupled plasma (ICP) etching, slow ICP etching and piranha treatment, the unreliable surface of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta-\text{Ga}2\mathrm{O}_{3}$</tex> can be effectively removed with small surface roughness and little co-products, thus increasing BV from 141 V to 724 V and reducing <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R_{on,sp}$</tex> from 5.1 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{m}\Omega\cdot \text{cm}^{2}$</tex> to 1.2 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{m}\Omega\cdot \text{cm}^{2}$</tex>. Consequently, the results validate the effectiveness of the surface treatments and can provide guidance for device process optimization.

articleTitle: Demonstration of Pseudo Independent Driving of Buried Gate in Trench Field Plate MOSFETs
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: We have proposed pseudo independent driving technique of Gate and buried Field Plate (FP) gate in a Trench Field Plate Power MOSFET (Trench FP MOSFET). Proposed method is expected to low conduction loss due to biased buried FP gate as well as a Gate-connected buried FP gate (Gate FP) and high-speed switching as well as a Source-connected buried FP gate (Source FP) by using only three additional components and this module behaves like a conventional three-terminal power MOSFET. In this paper, we experimentally demonstrated static characteristics and dynamic switching performances of this pseudo independent driving. We fabricated proposed pseudo driving module with discrete components on DBC (Direct Bonded Copper) substrate. Breakdown voltage and diode characteristics of this module were comparable to the Source FP and the Gate FP. On-resistance of this module was lower than the Source FP and the same as the Gate FP. Turn-on and turn-off period of this module became shorter than the Gate FP and were almost comparable to the Source FP.

Author Keywords: Pseudo independent buried FP gate driving

articleTitle: Design and Development of p-GaN Gate HEMT with Schottky Source Extension for Improved Short-Circuit Reliability
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: This study investigates the p-GaN gate HEMT with Schottky source extension (SSE) for improved short-circuit (SC) reliability. Under higher drain bias, the SSE pinches off and functions as a current source, resulting in reduced saturation current <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(I_{\text{D,sat}})$</tex> that is expected to enhance the short-circuit reliability. According to TCAD simulation, compared to other approaches (i.e. reducing <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{\text{GS}}$</tex> or using a larger <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$L_{\mathrm{G}}$</tex>), the adoption of SSE only slightly sacrifices its <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R$</tex><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ON</inf> for a targeted <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I_{\text{D,sat}}$</tex>. Fabricated devices with and without SSE are evaluated for SC reliability. The high-voltage pulse <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I_{\mathrm{D}}-V_{\text{DS}}$</tex> test mimics the SC stress, and the new device with SSE can endure an SC pulse with much higher <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{\text{DS}}$</tex>. The progressive SC-stress/ <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I_{\text{OFF}}$</tex> characterization monitors the accumulative SC degradation of devices, confirming that the new device with SSE is much more rugged against SC-stress. Therefore, the proposed p-GaN gate HEMT with SSE offers a promising approach for developing SC-rugged GaN power transistors for industrial applications.

articleTitle: Enhanced Gate Breakdown in β-Ga2O3HJFET through a NiOx/GaOxp-n Junction Gate Stack
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: In this work, we explore a novel structure of p-n herterojunction field-effect transistors (PN-HJFETs) to enhance gate breakdown characteristics. A sputtering n- <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{GaO}_{\mathrm{x}}/\mathrm{p}-\text{NiO}_{\mathrm{x}}$</tex> stack was featured as the gate of PN-HJFETs, showing improved gate breakdown capability. Schottky HJFETs (S-HJFETs) were fabricated as comparisons with PN-HJFET. Results demonstrate that PN-HJFETs exhibit ultra-low threshold voltage shifts, significantly small gate leakage, and enhanced forward gate breakdown voltage, surpassing the performance of S-HJFET. Moreover, PN-HJFETs exhibit excellent stability at high temperatures. Mechanism analysis suggests a hopping mechanism prevailing in low voltage regions and Poole Frenkel emission dominating in relatively high voltage region. Output characteristics and breakdown voltage measurements further validate the efficacy of HJFETs. Overall, the fabricated PN-HJFET structure shows promising potential for high-power and high-frequency switching applications.

articleTitle: Automotive Application Relevant Failure Mechanisms Under Cyclic Thermo-Mechanical Load
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: The change to wide bandgap power semiconductors in automotive traction inverters enables higher operation temperature and also higher temperature swings. The existing packaging technology for the bare dies comprising soldering and Al wire bonding cannot withstand the accompanying higher thermo-mechanical loads. This leads to the need of new die-related packaging technologies. Two possible new packaging technologies for silicon carbide and gallium nitride devices - namely, sintering and embedding - and their relevant failure mechanisms will be investigated using power cycling experiments.

articleTitle: Superjunction MOSFET with an N-Dot Region in the P-Pillar for Soft Reverse Recovery
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: In this paper, a novel superjunction MOSFET with an N-dot region in the P-pillar is proposed and experimentally investigated. By taking advantage of the difference in diffusion rates of boron and arsenic, the N-dot region is naturally formed by implanting equal doses of arsenic and boron after the P-pillar implantation. Therefore, the charge balance condition between the N-pillar and the P-pillar remains unchanged, which allows an unaffected breakdown voltage of the proposed superjunction MOSFET. More importantly, the N-dot region increases the grounding resistance of the P-pillar located below the N-dot region, which reduces the extraction velocity of the non-equilibrium holes during the reverse recovery period. Consequently, a soft reverse recovery performance is obtained in the proposed one. The experiment results show that, in comparison with the conventional superjunction MOSFET, the softness factor of the proposed one could be improved by more than 2.5 times without side effects.

articleTitle: Design and Fabrication of Low-Leakage Vertical GaN TMBS Rectifier with Low Forward Voltage Drop
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: In this work, the vertical GaN trench MIS barrier Schottky (TMBS) rectifier was developed to reduce the leakage current density of the Schottky barrier diode. The vertical GaN TMBS rectifier was fabricated with self-aligned insulator opening process, in order to eliminate the gap between trench and Schottky edge (L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TS</inf>). The L<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TS</inf> is induced by the mask-aligned insulator opening process, which would result in the peak electric field at the edge of Schottky contact on the mesa, leading to increased reverse leakage current. This work studies the influence of the TMBS structure on the device's performance. As mesa width narrows, the reverse leakage current density decreases and the breakdown voltage increases, due to the suppressed electric field at the Schottky interface and at the corner of the trench bottom. The vertical GaN TMBS rectifier exhibits the breakdown voltage of ~810 V and the leakage current density of ~10-<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup> A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Furthermore, the forward conduction performance can be improved with hexagonal cell in contrast to the stripe cell, showing the moderate forward voltage drop of ~1 V. Besides, the high-temperature performances (up to 200°C) are also presented. These results show that the vertical GaN TMBS diode have great potential for the high-power-density and high-efficiency power electronic applications.

articleTitle: Avalanche Stability Improvement by Boron Implanted GaN JTE Structures with Reduced Trap Density
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: In this work, we examined improvement of vertical GaN p-n diodes with boron-implanted junction termination extension (JTE), focusing on breakdown voltage stability under avalanche stress. In the JTE technique, acceptors in the p-type epitaxial layer are compensated to achieve charge balance by introducing donor levels caused by boron implantation. We demonstrate significant suppression of avalanche walkout for 1.2 kV p-n diodes with the JTE structure and high temperature annealing of up to 900 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">${}^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex> to reduce deep trap density after the implantation. The p-n diodes fabricated with the new process condition on 4-inch freestanding GaN substrates demonstrate good reverse characteristics over the entire wafer and high avalanche capability with positive temperature coefficient of breakdown voltage.

articleTitle: 1-kV β-Ga2O3UMOSFET with Quasi-Inversion Nitrogen-Ion-Implanted Channel
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: In this work, 1-kV vertical enhancement-mode <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta- \text{Ga}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3}$</tex> U-shaped trench gate metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistors (UMOSFETs) with nitrogen-ion-implanted channel have been successfully demonstrated. The nitrogen-ion-implanted region serves as a current blocking layer (CBL) and also allows a quasi-inversion channel to form at the trench sidewall. The activation annealing temperature of the nitrogen-ion-implanted CBL was optimized to suppress the leakage current. The CBL annealed at 1150 °C exhibits better current blocking capability than its 1100 °C annealed counterpart. Based on the CBL annealed at 1150 °C, the UMOSFET exhibits an improved on-off ratio of ~ 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup>, an on-resistance of 87.6 mΩ-cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>and a remarkable breakdown voltage of 1028 V. This is the first 1-kV <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta-\text{Ga}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3}$</tex> MOSFET based on CBL, showing the potential <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{of}\beta-\text{Ga}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3}$</tex> UMOSFETs with N-implanted channel for kilovolt-class applications.

articleTitle: Vertical Leakage and Back-Gating Characteristics of GaN HEMTs Based on GaN/AlN Epitaxy on Off-Axis Conducting 4H-SiC
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: As wide-bandgap semiconductors, GaN and SiC have been regarded as silicon's successors in a wide range of power electronic applications and developed independently for decades. The mainstream GaN and SiC-based power devices exhibit complementary merits and drawbacks, which sparks the effort to integrate them on a single platform. This work studies a feasible configuration in GaN/SiC integration, with GaN-based heterojunction epi-structure to be grown on off-axis and conducting 4H-SiC substrates. The vertical leakage and back-gating characteristics of GaN high-electron-mobility transistors (HEMTs) made on GaN/AlN epitaxy on off-axis 4H-SiC substrates with different surface doping are investigated. It is revealed that the conducting SiC substrates can inject both electrons and holes into the GaN/AlN epi-layer above. The presence of the AlN transition layer on SiC is speculated as the major cause for such phenomena as its constituent elements, Al and N, can act as acceptor and donor in SiC, respectively.

Index Terms: Gallium Nitride High Electron Mobility Transistors

articleTitle: Monolithic Integration of D/E-Mode Tri-Gate AlGaN/GaN MIS-HEMTs for Power ICs
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: This study presents the experimental validation of the integrated circuits based on DIE-mode tri-gate GaN MIS-HEMTs. The threshold voltage of the devices can be modulated from -9.1 V to +1.1 V by varying the fin width from 800 nm to 56 nm on a single chip. The E-mode device exhibits a slight threshold voltage shift <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\Delta \mathrm{V}_{\text{th}})$</tex> of -0.11 V from room temperature up to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$15 0^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex>. At fin width of 56 nm, an E-mode device shows a low on-resistance <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{R}_{\text{on}})$</tex> of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$8.2 \Omega.\text{mm}$</tex>, an on/off current ratio exceeding 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">9</sup>, and a breakdown voltage (VBR) of 1439 V. Furthermore, the monolithically integrated inverter has stable dynamic characteristics at 1 MHz. The inverter shows a logic low noise margin <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{N}_{\text{ML}})$</tex> of 2.04 V at a supply voltage of 10 V and a logic high noise margin <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{N}_{\text{MH}})$</tex> of 6.83 V. The threshold voltage of the inverter <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{V}_{\text{th,inv}})$</tex> exhibits a variation of 0.09 V up to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$15 0^{\circ}\mathrm{C}$</tex>. These results validate the viability of monolithic integration of tri-gate GaN, thereby offering a significant opportunity to develop high-frequency and compact power conversion systems.

articleTitle: Study of a Packaging Technology for Ultra Compact Double-Side Cooled Power Module with Power Chip Size Package
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: In response to the demand for higher power density of inverters for EVs, we are developing package technology to take advantage of the excellent high-speed switching performance and high-power density of SiC-MOSFETs to the limit of their characteristics. In this study, we have focused on developing the following four key technologies to realize low height, downsizing, and high efficiency 1200 V/200 A 2-in-1 double-side cooled power module technology. A) SiC-MOSFET mounted power chip size package technology, B) cooling fin and case integrated insulation substrate technology, C) bump bonding technology to absorb height variation occurs in mounting areas on both sides of chips, and D) insulation technology inside double-side cooled power modules. These four key technologies have also made it possible to simplify the complex structure and assembly process of double-side cooled power modules. Furthermore, we evaluated the static, switching, and thermal resistance characteristics and confirmed that the developed double-side cooled power module performs as expected.

articleTitle: Versatile Dynamic On-Resistance Test Bench for GaN Power Transistors with Considerations for Soft and Hard Switching, Time-Resolved Test, Packaged and On-Wafer Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: In this work, we develop a dynamic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R_{\text{ON}}$</tex> test bench for GaN HEMT based on two half-bridge pulse generating circuits, enabling versatile selection of soft switching (SSW) and hard switching (HSW) test, allowing long-duration test, and supporting both packaged large-area devices and on-wafer small-size devices. For packaged devices, under SSW test, Schottky-gate p-GaN HEMT (SG-HEMT) exhibit a bell-shaped dynamic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R_{\text{ON}}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{\text{DS}}$</tex> curve, while the ohmic-gate p-GaN HEMT (GIT) and Si superjunction (SJ-) MOSFET exhibit stable dynamic RON. Under HSW test, the dynamic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R_{\text{ON}}$</tex> of SG-HEMT and GIT are both slightly higher than SSW test. The hard-switching energy <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(E_{\text{HSW}})$</tex> is controlled by a capacitor C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">HSW</inf>. During 1-hour continuous SSW and HSW test, the dynamic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R_{\text{ON}}$</tex> of GaN HEMT increases gradually and saturates. The on-wafer device in this work is an active-passivation HEMT (AP-HEMT) with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$W_{\mathrm{G}}=10 \mu \mathrm{m}$</tex>. The SSW dynamic RON of AP-HEMT, extracted with a delay time of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 20\ \mu \mathrm{s}$</tex>, is comparable to that of the-state-of-the-art commercial GaN transistor using the same testing condition.

articleTitle: A High-Speed Dual-NMOSFETs Output Stage Buffer with Charge-Transferring Bootstrap Circuit for GaN-Based DToF LiDAR Application
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: In GaN-based direct time-of-flight LiDAR system, a dual-NMOSFETs output stage buffer with charge-transferring bootstrap (CTB) circuit is proposed to enhance driving capability and transmission speed of GaN driver by voltage boosting of CTB circuit. A LDMOS-less high-voltage level shifter is also provided to ensure high speed of proposed buffer. The buffer has been fabricated in a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0.18\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex> BCD process as part of a GaN driver. Experimental results show that the GaN driver with proposed buffer operates at 50MHz pulse repetition frequency (PRF) with 1.4ns on-time, where the rise/fall time of output pulse are 323ps/333ps and turn on/off delay are 2.41ns/2.56ns. The GaN driver with proposed buffer has stronger driving capability and higher transmission speed than a GaN driver with the same peak source & sink currents.

articleTitle: Split-Gate CSTBT™ for Suppression of Negative Gate Capacitance Under Short Circuit
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: CSTBT™ can reduce on-state voltage drop <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{V}_{\text{CEsat}})$</tex> by storing carriers. On the other hand, storing carriers causes flow of displacement current <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{I}_{\text{dis}})$</tex> into the gate, resulting in the overshoot of the gate-emitter voltage (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">GE</inf>). The phenomenon of IGBTs is expressed as a negative gate capacitance. In this study, we have found a solution to suppress the negative gate capacitance for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{CSTBT}^{\text{TM}}$</tex>, enabling the reduction in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{V}_{\text{CEsat}}$</tex> by using a split-gate structure. Additionally, we have clarified the mechanism through a combination of measurements and device simulations. As a result, the split-gate achieved 76% reduction in integral of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{I}_{\text{dis}}$</tex> at the same <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{V}_{\text{CEsat}}$</tex> compared to the conventional structure. This is because most of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{I}_{\text{dis}}$</tex> flowing to lower split gate is directed towards the emitter.

articleTitle: Reducing turn-Off loss by suppressing Back-Side parasitic npn Transistor in Single-Back and Double-Front Gate-Controlled IGBT
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: Reducing turn-off loss <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(E_{\text{off}_{-}\text{total}})$</tex> in insulated-gate bipolar transistors (IGBTs) improves the power consumption of high-power converter systems. Multi-gate IGBTs can reduce <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E_{\text{off}_{-}\text{total}}$</tex> because stored carriers are reduced by adding independently controllable gates that switch just before the turn-off period. The single-back and double-front gate-controlled IGBT (SDG-IGBT) reduces <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E_{\text{off}_{-}\text{total}}$</tex> when both the control gate (CG) on the emitter side and the back gate (BG) on the collector side are operated simultaneously. As the issue, a parasitic npn transistor on back-side decreases injection efficiency. The fabricated 4.5-kV class SDG-IGBT with deep p layer (DP) successfully decrease <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{\text{ce}(\text{sat})}$</tex> by suppressing operation of a parasitic effects. Moreover, we clarify that the tradeoff between <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{\text{ce}(\text{sat})}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta E_{\text{off}_{-}\text{total}}$</tex> in mode-3 are improved because the storage carriers around BG is increased. In mode-2, The BG and CG can be redesigned individually, because the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta E_{\text{off}_{-}\text{total}}$</tex> to mode-1 is almost the same between with and without DP. As the result, SDG-IGBT with DP achieves to reduce <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E_{\text{off}_{-}\text{total}}$</tex> in mode-4.

articleTitle: Compact SPICE Modeling of Total Ionizing Dose for Shield Gate Trench MOSFET
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: This paper develops a compact SPICE model of total ionizing dose (TID) for shield gate trench (SGT) MOSFETs, including a channel current, a drift region current and three external capacitances. The channel current is modeled by the simplified BSIM4, while the drift region current including velocity saturation describes the depletion caused by shield gate. The external capacitances adopt behavior models to facilitate the fitting of the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Q_{\mathrm{G}}$</tex> curves. In order to build the TID degradation model for the device, this paper explores the relationship between the oxide trap density in the channel and the drift region and the TID dose, external biases. Based on this relationship, the functions of various model parameters with respect to TID dose and external biases are proposed, enabling the proposed compact SPICE model to accurately capture the I-V and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Q_{\mathrm{G}}$</tex> characteristics under different TID doses. The experimental data demonstrate that the proposed model has ability to characterize the TID degradation of SGT MOSFETs.

articleTitle: Durable Edge Termination Design of SiC SBD Against Humidity
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: Humidity robustness of SiC devices has become a major concern. The degradation of SiC devices under high temperature and high humidity conditions is expected to be caused by excessive electric fields in the termination region. In this study, accelerated high voltage high humidity high temperature reverse bias tests are conducted on 3.3 kV SiC-SBDs with field limiting rings of different electric field designs. The results confirm that reducing the electric field on the SiC surface improves the durability of the SiC devices against humidity.

articleTitle: Experimental Comparative Demonstrations and Analysis of 3.3kV 4H-SiC Common-Drain and Common-Source Bidirectional Charge-Balanced Power DMOSFETs Switching
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: In this work, we evaluate the switching performance of a hybrid bidirectional (BD) 3.3kV 4H-SiC Charge-Balanced (CB) power DMOSFET in common-drain (CD) and common-source (CS) configurations. Based on the experimental data, we develop an RC switching model and use it to compare the switching performance of the BD CB DMOSFET for the CD and CS configurations.

articleTitle: 2.7 kVβ- Ga2O3 Heterojunction Barrier Schottky Diode with Low Leakage Current < 1 mA/cm2 Based upon RESURF Effect
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: In this paper, we present vertical <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta-\text{Ga}2\mathrm{O}_{3}$</tex> heterojunction barrier Schottky diodes (HJBSDs) with variable width (W) of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{p}+$</tex> region to optimize the forward and reverse characteristics of devices. The bipolar operation mode of HJBSDs leads to a decreasing specific on-resistance <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(R_{\mathrm{o}\mathrm{n},\mathrm{s}\mathrm{p}})$</tex> as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$W$</tex> increases. The reverse leakage current in all HJBSDs is significantly suppressed thanks to the reduced surface field (RESURF) effect arising from junction barrier Schottky structure. Furthermore, a floating field rings structure is employed to reduce the electric field at the edge of anode and achieve a high breakdown voltage. A highest breakdown voltage of 2.74 kV with a low leakage current of less than 1 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{mA}/\text{cm}^{2}$</tex> and a low <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R_{\mathrm{o}\mathrm{n},\mathrm{s}\mathrm{p}}$</tex> of 7.5 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{m}\Omega\cdot \text{cm}^{2}$</tex> were achieved in HJBSD with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$W$</tex> of 15μm, yielding a superior power figure-of-merit of 1. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$0\text{GW}/\text{cm}^{2}$</tex>. This work provides valuable insights into reducing off-state losses for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta-\text{Ga}_2\mathrm{O}_{3}$</tex> power devices.

articleTitle: Digital Twin-Based Lifetime Estimation of SiC Power Modules
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: This research paper describes the reliability investigation of devices with SiC die on substrates and their lifetime estimation based on digital twin methodology. The most common failure modes that occur in power modules during power cycling and thermal cycling are bond wire degradation, die attach failures or system solder deterioration. The digital twin-based lifetime estimation helps to calculate the lifetime of power devices based on variable input parameters like temperature swing or minimum junction temperature of the chip etc. for example. This method develops a meta model of optimal prognosis file (MOP). It is shown that the inputs can be varied and the corresponding lifetime can be predicted.

articleTitle: Comparative Study on Power Cycling Capabilities of SiC Power MOSFET and Si IGBT Baseplate-Less Power Modules
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: This paper presents a comparative study on power cycling (PC) capabilities of SiC power MOSFET and Si IGBT baseplate-less power modules with sintered and solder die <sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">a</sup>ttach, based on PC experiments and electro-thermo-mechanical (ETM) simulations. A comprehensive failure analysis after the PC confirms that the bond wire degradation occurred for all modules. However, only SiC power MOSFET modules with solder die attach showed significantly lower PC lifetime, and failed by solder degradation as dominant failure mode. Even though a shorter lifetime can be expected for SiC power MOSFET modules due to higher Young's modulus of SiC, a comparable PC lifetime of the SiC power MOSFET modules with sintered die attach and the Si IGBT modules with both solder and sintered die attach was achieved. Using the ETM simulations, this was attributed to significant effects of current density and wire geometry on bond wire lift-off. Furthermore, the results point out that the available lifetime models proposed for Si IGBT and SiC power MOSFETs modules have to be revisited.

articleTitle: Improvement of the RON- BV Tradeoff in Field-Plate MOSFETs by Localized Fixed Charges in the Trench Oxide
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: With the increasing demand for low-voltage power MOSFETs in applications such as data centers, the need to reduce power losses is also growing. Aiming to decrease conduction loss, we investigate a method for improving the tradeoff between the on-resistance <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(R_{\text{ON}})$</tex> and breakdown voltage (BV) of field-plate (FP) MOSFETs by using localized and fixed positive charges (LFCs) in the trench oxide. The simulation results show that BV is improved when the LFC density peak is at the trench-bottom oxide because the LFCs relax the trench-bottom electric field. In addition, the LFCs contribute to the reduction in RON because the electrons accumulate on the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Si}/\text{SiO}_{2}$</tex> surface, and the spreading resistance is reduced. A gradient LFC profile was realized in the experiment by applying proton irradiation, which enabled some of the oxygen vacancies in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{SiO}_{2}$</tex> to act as positive fixed charges. The experimental results imply that the gradient LFC is useful in the trench oxide for improving the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R_{\text{ON}}-BV$</tex> tradeoff, particularly without any disruption of the charge balance.

articleTitle: A 2.2MHz GaN Switching Power IC with Auto-Phase-Aligned EMI Adaptive Self-Cancellation and BER-Conscious Adaptive SSM for Autonomous Driving Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: To address stringent electromagnetic interference (EMI) requirements in autonomous driving applications, this paper presents a gallium nitride (GaN) boost converter with adaptive EMI controls for enhanced system reliability and communication safety. To address the challenges by drastic operation condition changes, an on-chip adaptive self-cancellation (ASC) technique is proposed to achieve input current ripple cancellation, thereby reducing EMI dynamically. Additionally, an auto-phase-aligned control method enhances ripple cancellation precision, further improving EMI performance. The paper also presents an adaptive spread-spectrum modulation (SSM) with controlled spread range <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\Delta _{fSW})$</tex> to prevent a potential increase in bit error rate (BER) while achieving adaptive EMI suppression. Experimental validation involves the fabrication of a 2.2-MHz GaN power IC prototype in a 180-nm BCD process, demonstrating a 7.5-fold adaptive reduction in input ripple with the ASC technique, in response to 1.5 times input voltage change and 2 times output voltage change. When combined with adaptive SSM, an overall EMI suppression of 16 dB is achieved at 2.2 MHz, meeting the automotive CISPR 25 Class 5 standard.

articleTitle: Degradation Behavior of SiC Trench MOSFETs by Total-Ionizing-dose Irradiation Under Gate Voltage Stress
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: SiC MOSFETs total-ionizing-dose TID tolerance are highly related to the structure and the strength of the gate electric field. The primary failure mechanism is the accumulation of radiation-induced charges in the gate oxide layer, which results in a significant threshold voltage shift. SiC trench-gate MOSFETs display markedly lower TID tolerance (below 60 krad) compared to planar type, asymmetric devices exhibit the largest threshold voltage shift <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{\text{TH}}$</tex>, and double-trench devices show the greatest degradation in on resistance <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R_{\text{ON}}$</tex>, which is related to the thicker oxide layer and inferior interface radiation resistance. A high electric field above 2 MV/cm can diminish the oxide trap charges accumulation by hole capture cross-section reduce, thereby improving the TID tolerance of SiC MOSFETs.

articleTitle: Investigation into Relationship of the Switching Performance and Short-Circuit Withstand Time on 1.2 kV 4H-SiC Power MOSFETs
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: The reduction of on-resistance of SiC devices contributes to the reduction in conduction losses and increased ampacity along with switching speed benefit of the wide band gap nature of the material. However, on-resistance improvement results in a tradeoff relationship with short-circuit withstand time, switching energy losses due to various factors, including parasitic capacitances. In this paper, we report the results of our investigation into the relationship between on-resistance, breakdown voltage, parasitic capacitance, short-circuit withstand time, and switching energy loss by varying device design and process parameters. Finally, these results show that it is possible to achieve better overall trade by adjusting both design and process parameters for an optimized SiC MOSFET.

articleTitle: A 900V HVIC Process with New Structure of Internal Bootstrap Diode
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: This paper proposes a high-voltage integrated circuit (HVIC) process that includes an internal bootstrap diode (BSD) with a new structure, consisting of a diode and a resistor region without a gate control unit. While using the proposed structure without a gate control structure, the forward current can be improved about 20% due to the short current path. The ultra-high voltage (UHV) process that will be introduced in this paper includes the integrated BSD which operation voltage is from 600 to 900V.

articleTitle: 3D Co-packaging of GaN/SiC Cascode Device for High-Frequency Power Switching Operation
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: To unlock the full potential of GaN/SiC cascode device in fast switching capability, the parasitic inductances of interconnections should be reduced. In this work, enabled by the planar nature of the GaN HEMT, a compact 3D co-packaging solution with greatly reduced interconnection inductances is proposed. Compared with the latest commercially available SiC MOSFETs and the Si/SiC cascode devices, the GaN/SiC cascode device in the 3D co-packaged configuration delivers the fastest switching process with lowest switching loss, making it highly preferred for high-frequency power switching applications.

articleTitle: 3.3 kV-Class 4H-SiC Epi-Refilled Super-Junction Diode with Repetitive Surge Current Robustness
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: In this paper, the 4H-SiC super-junction (SJ) Schottky barrier diode (SBD) with hexagonal cell has been fabricated by trench etching and epitaxial regrowth process. The fabricated device achieves a breakdown voltage (BV) of 3570V with specific on-resistance <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{R}_{\text{on},\text{sp}})$</tex> of 4.5mΩ.cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>which breaks the one-dimensional performance limit of the SiC unipolar device. The impact of SJ's mesa width on static I-V and C-V characteristic has also been investigated. With a double pulse test, the fabricated device performs high speed switching over 50kV/μs. The repetitive surge current test is also carried out on the fabricated device to demonstrate its surge robustness.

articleTitle: A Physics-Oriented Analysis of SiC Trench MOSFETs Under Gate Switching Stress Test Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: This work presents a physics-oriented investigation on SiC MOSFET dynamic stress in the recently required Gate Switching Stress (GSS) test.
