Differently from precedent works, TCAD physics-based simulations are calibrated with real measurements in 1200V SiC Trench MOSFETs by a dedicated GSS test setup. The calibrated models are used to dynamically inspect the physical magnitudes during GSS turn-on under different test conditions and to better understand the GSS stressors for the subsequent Gate Switching Instability (GSI).

articleTitle: Elucidation of New Turn-on Voltage Tail Phenomenon of IGBT and Improvement by Dynamic-CSL Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: The voltage tail phenomenon during IGBTs turn-on is one of the causes of the increase in turn-on loss (Eon). It has been reported that the voltage tail during turn-on can be suppressed by reducing C<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">gc</inf>, however, we have confirmed that there is a voltage tail phenomenon that cannot be explained by the effect of Cgc alone. To figure out the voltage tail phenomenon during turn-on, it is necessary to understand the 3D carrier behavior and experimentally demonstrate. In this study, we elucidate that this phenomenon is caused by the strong 3D carrier behavior using 3D-TCAD and propose a structure to solve this problem. In the proposed structure, the channel P layer directly below the source has the same accepter concentration as conventional structure, but the dynamic current spreading layer (Dynamic-CSL) where there is no source has a lower acceptor concentration layer. This Dynamic-CSL improves the 3D carrier transport. The voltage tail and Eon were significantly reduced in the proposed structure. We elucidated the voltage tail phenomenon during turn-on, which could not be fully explained by 2D-TCAD analysis, and we could experimentally demonstrate the reduction of voltage tail.

articleTitle: Heteroepitaxial $\epsilon-\text{Ga}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3}$ MOSFETs on a 4-inch Sapphire Substrate with a Power Figure of Merit of 0.29 $\text{GW}/\text{cm}^{2}$
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: We have designed and fabricated a high-voltage metal-oxide-semiconductor field effect transistor (MOSFET) based on heteroepitaxial <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varepsilon-\text{Ga}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3}$</tex>. The high-quality unintentionally-doped (UID) <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varepsilon-\text{Ga}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3}$</tex> film was grown by metalorganic chemical vapor deposition (MOCVD) on a 4-inch sapphire substrate. Through an optimized fluorine-plasma treatment process, we achieved high-density surface doping with a carrier sheet density <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(n_{s})$</tex> exceeding <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$10^{14}\text{cm}^{-2}$</tex> and mobility of 32 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{cm}^{2}/\mathrm{V}\cdot \mathrm{s}$</tex>. We proposed a dual-density channel design for the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varepsilon, \text{Ga}_2\mathrm{O}_{3}$</tex> MOSFETs, which involved high-density doping in the access region to reduce the parasitic resistance and low-density doping under the gate to ensure device pitch-off. This concept was verified using TCAD simulation before device fabrication. The fabricated <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\varepsilon-\text{Ga}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3}$</tex> MOSFETs, with a gate-to-drain spacing <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(L_{GD})$</tex> of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$10 [\iota \mathrm{m}$</tex>, exhibited a high breakdown voltage <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(V_{br})$</tex> of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2.85 \text{kV}$</tex> and a specific on-resistance <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(R_{on,sp})$</tex> of 27.6 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{m}\Omega\cdot \text{cm}^{2}$</tex>, yielding a power figure of merit (PFOM) of 0.29 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{GW}/\text{cm}^{2}$</tex>. This PFOM value is the highest reported value for heteroepitaxial <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Ga}_2\mathrm{O}_{3}$</tex> devices and among the best in homoepitaxial <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta-\text{Ga}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3}$</tex> lateral FETs.

articleTitle: Development of Vertical-Channel Fin-SiC MOSFET for 3.3 kV Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: We have developed a 3.3 kV SiC Vertical-Channel Fin MOSFET, original structure named VC Fin-SiC. The JFET structure was optimized using TCAD simulation to achieve low on-resistance and high reliability. Our evaluation of the static and switching properties demonstrate that VC Fin-SiC can achieve low on-resistance with high threshold voltage and small switching loss with fast turn-on even for high voltage applications thanks to its structural superiority.

articleTitle: A Novel Gate Driver with Charge Sharing Technique to Optimize Gate Turn-On/Turn-Off Overshoot and Switching Loss Trade-off in SiC Power MOSFETs
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: This paper proposes a charge sharing approach to optimize gate turn-on/turn-off overshoot and switching loss trade-off in SiC Power MOSFETs. The proposed technique achieves significant reductions in overshoot ratios while maintaining similar switching losses compared to conventional methods. Specifically, the proposed technique reduces turn-off overshoot ratio by 57% with only a 30% increase in turn-off switching loss <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{o}\mathrm{f}\mathrm{f}})$</tex> and turn-on overshoot ratio by 39% with only a 27% increase in turn-on switching loss <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{E}_{\mathrm{o}\mathrm{n}})$</tex>. Moreover, when driving modules with large input capacitance <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathrm{C}_{\mathfrak{m}\mathrm{o}\mathrm{d}\mathrm{u}\mathrm{I}\mathrm{e}})$</tex>, the charge sharing method decreases overshoot ratio by 38% during turn-off and by 23% during turn-on, with minimal impact on switching loss. The results show that using the charge sharing technique can improve the performance of SiC power MOSFETs in power electronics applications.

articleTitle: Novel Methodology for Fast Model Parameter Extracting Using $Q_{\mathrm{g}}$ Waveforms to Accurately Capture Switching Characteristics of SiC MOSFET Under Various Load Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: This paper proposes a method for fast extracting model parameters, which can accurately capture the switching characteristics of SiC MOSFETs under various load conditions. The power limitation of the experimental instrument makes it difficult to obtain <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I-V$</tex> data under high <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{\mathrm{d}\mathrm{s}}$</tex>, so the proposed method extracts this data from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$Q_{\mathrm{g}}$</tex> waveforms. In addition, the presented method abandons fitting <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C-V$</tex> curves and instead fits the curves of charge change <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Delta Q_{\mathrm{g}}$</tex> on the gate with respect to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{\text{ds}}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{\text{gs}}$</tex> to extract the capacitance parameters of the model, thereby solving the issue where the “Miller ramp” cannot be captured in existing models. This paper writes the model into PSPICE and utilizes the proposed method to extract the model parameters. The experimental data confirms that the proposed method outperforms existing methods in characterizing switching waveforms of SiC MOSFETs.

articleTitle: LDMOS of 34mΩ-cm2 On-Resistance with 700V Breakdown Voltage
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: We have designed and fabricated an Accumulation Lateral Diffused MOSFET (LDMOS) (AccuMOS®), which incorporates multiple electrodes over drift region and regulated by an integrated circuit (IC). A record low specific <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{R}_{\text{dson}}$</tex> of 34mΩ-cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> with breakdown voltage (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">B</inf>) of 700V has been obtained. Devices were tested in switching power applications and performance was satisfactory. Current LDMOS structure is scalable and performance is expected to progress with smaller lithographic features. Analysis suggests a 3-dimensional fin-FET structure could potentially reduce <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{R}_{\text{dson}}$</tex> to below 6mΩ-cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{V}_{\mathrm{B}}=700\mathrm{V}$</tex>.

articleTitle: Enhancement-Mode P-Channel GaN/InAlN T-Shaped FinFETs with ION> 60 mA/mm and Adjustable VTH of −0.7 V – −3.1 V
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: In this letter, we present high-performance enhancement-mode (E-mode) p-channel T-shaped Fin Field-Effect Transistors (FinFETs) fabricated on a proposed p-GaN/ AlN/InAlN epitaxial structure. A T-shaped Fin with a smooth and steep sidewall was achieved by utilizing electron-beam lithography and anisotropic sidewall wet etching in tetramethyl ammonium hydroxide (TMAH) solution. A low ohmic contact resistance <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(R_{\mathrm{C}})$</tex> of 11.6 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\Omega .mm$</tex> was attained by using Ti mask process. Moreover, the devices exhibited a high on-current density (I<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ON</inf>) of 61.5 mA/mm and a high ON-OFF current ratio <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(I_{\text{ON}}/I_{\text{OFF}})$</tex> of 5 ×10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup>. An adjustable threshold voltage (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TH</inf>) of −0.7 V – −3.1 V was achieved by controlling the width of the Fin, which can be preferably used to match n-channel GaN devices for GaN CMOS design. Compared with the reported p-channel GaN FETs on HEMT platforms, especially the E-mode FETs, the fabricated devices show more excellent performance in terms of ION, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{\text{TH}}$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$R_{\text{ON}}$</tex>. These results unveil the excellent prospects of the fabricated devices for future monolithic integration of GaN-based logic and power applications.

articleTitle: Analysis of Leakage Mechanism in Irradiated 4H-SiC INV and NOR Logic Gate Circuits
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: The performance degradation of 4H-SiC CMOS devices, inverter (INV), and NOR logic gate circuits under irradiation are examined in this paper. It is noted that the leakage current of INV and NOR gate circuits is much higher than the summary leakage of NMOS and PMOS at a total irradiation dose of 300kGy, which indicates an extra leakage current path in INV and NOR gate circuits. The reason for leakage current is elucidated through Emission Microscope (EMMI) testing and analysis of leakage paths based on the layout. After irradiation, an inversion layer forms on the P-epi surface beneath the polysilicon gate and VDD metal, leading to electron leakage current from N-well to P-epi. At last, recommendations for enhancing the radiation tolerance of 4H-SiC CMOS gate circuits are proposed. Simulation verification using T -CAD tools has validated the effectiveness of this reinforcement method in substantially reducing both types of additional leakage.

articleTitle: Improved Gate ESD Behaviors of p-GaN Power HEMTs by Hybrid Gate Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: The Floating Island (FI) technology is a promising approach to break the 1D theoretical limit of the power semiconductor devices. However, the Floating Island is confronted with severe turn-on recovery problem due to residue charges in oppositely doped regions after blocking state. In this paper, a novel N+ Buffer is conceived as a solution to the turn-on recovery problem. The SiC Floating Island Schottky Barrier Diode with N+ Buffer (NB-FISBD) is experimentally fabricated and tested. It shows high static performance and effectively suppressed turn-on recovery problem. The NB-FISBD is expected to help the Floating Island devices unleash their potential in power electronic systems.

articleTitle: 900V Normally-OFF GaN-on-Si Transistors Achieved by Substrate Potential Modulation (SPM)
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: A 900-V normally-OFF GaN-on-Si transistor is demonstrated on a 650-V p-GaN-gate platform using substrate potential modulation method, without any additional EPI or process adjustment. The integration scheme can modulate the Si substrate potential between floating and grounded status, as the transistor switches from high-voltage OFF-state to low-voltage ON-state. The proposed device can simultaneously deliver higher breakdown voltage and acceptable dynamic performance. I-V and C-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V$</tex> characteristics have been obtained. Reliability evaluation has been conducted to prove the 900-V blocking capability. The working principle is explained with equivalent circuit model.

articleTitle: Fabrication and Optimization of a High-Reliability 700 V Super-Junction MOSFET with Segmented P-Buried RESURF Termination
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: In this work, we propose a 700 V super-junction MOSFET with segmented p-type buried RESURF (reduced surface field) layer (PBR) in the termination region. Due to the self-regulating effect of the RESURF structure and position of the PBR layer in the y-direction, we can obtain a more uniform surface electric field distribution and effectively alleviate the charge-imbalance issues in the termination region. Consequently, this results in a more stable breakdown voltage (BV) and enhances the reliability of the super-junction platform. Based on a multi-epitaxy/multi-implant platform, we conduct experiments with the optimized termination structure. The experimental devices demonstrate that BV of the proposed structure exceeding 750 V and specific on-resistance (R<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">ON,SP</inf>) below 1.5 Ω·mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, and the experimental results are in good consistence with the simulated results. The HTRB test results and shift curve of the experimental devices are also demonstrated in our work.

articleTitle: The Investigation on Diode Surge Current Capability of Reverse Conducting IGBT and The Impact of Gate Bias
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: In this work, third-quadrant I-V characteristics and surge current test are carried out on two commercial RC-IGBTs (DUT A and DUT B) under different gate bias (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">GE</inf>). The experimental results show that, compared to under -15V or OV gate bias, devices under +15V gate bias can result in 1) an increase in the on-state voltage drop under the same surge current, a decrease in 2) maximum bearable surge current and 3) maximum bearable surge energy of devices, which have an adverse effect on the surge tolerance of devices. Moreover, according to decapsulation analysis, for all devices under test, metal melting on chip surface is the main cause of surge failure. The surge current simulations show that current is more easily concentrated in monolithically integrated diodes under gate bias of +15V compared to -15V. Such a current distribution can lead to an increase in the voltage drop and more non-uniform heating of devices under +15V gate bias, resulting in a decrease of maximum bearable surge energy.

articleTitle: Substantial Improvement of the Short-circuit Capability of a 1.2 kV SiC MOSFET by a HfO2/SiO2 Ferroelectric Gate Stack
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: State-of-the-art Silicon Carbide (SiC) Metal Oxide Semiconductor Field Effect Transistors (MOSFETs) are required to meet strict constraints on short-circuit capability, that are challenging to achieve due to the limited volume of the device compared to the silicon counterpart. This paper presents a novel device concept for a 1.2 kV SiC MOSFET that harnesses the potential of a composite silicon oxide/ferroelectric gate stack. Simple modeling suggests that the Curie-Weiss dependence of the dielectric constant of the ferroelectric layer can counterbalance the current increase due to the temperature during short-circuit. TCAD simulations demonstrate a substantial short-circuit ruggedness improvement since the maximum temperature in the device during short circuit events is lower with respect to a reference device with a standard oxide gate dielectric by a factor ½.

articleTitle: Monolithically Integrated Power Converter Based on Etching-Free p-GaN HEMTs by Hydrogen Plasma Treatment Technology
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: This paper introduces a GaN power IC platform based on the novel hydrogen (H) plasma treatment technique to eliminate the p-GaN gate etch and improve device performance. A device advanced SPICE model (ASM) high-electron-mobility transistor (HEMT) is made and validated from experimental results. A monolithically integrated GaN power stage with gate driver is demonstrated for DC-DC converters, where the remaining components are discrete. The contributions of this paper may include 1) implementation of an etching-free hydrogen-treated p-GaN technology on a 4-inch wafer, enabling 10 A/800 V application; 2) design technology co-optimization (DTCO) via ASM simulation and experimental verification; 3) monolithic GaN IC with gate driver and power device used to a 48 V/1 V floating buck conversion. This work lays the foundation for the H-treated technology for smart all-GaN power systems.

articleTitle: 2kV SiC Floating Island SBD with N+ Buffer
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: The Floating Island (FI) technology is a promising approach to break the 1D theoretical limit of the power semiconductor devices. However, the Floating Island is confronted with severe turn-on recovery problem due to residue charges in oppositely doped regions after blocking state. In this paper, a novel N+ Buffer is conceived as a solution to the turn-on recovery problem. The SiC Floating Island Schottky Barrier Diode with N+ Buffer (NB-FISBD) is experimentally fabricated and tested. It shows high static performance and effectively suppressed turn-on recovery problem. The NB-FISBD is expected to help the Floating Island devices unleash their potential in power electronic systems.

articleTitle: Experimental and Theoretical Study on failure mechanism of Superjunction MOSFET under H3TRB Testing
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: H3TRB-HVDC test is the appropriate test to prove the robustness of chip against humidity and high electric fields. The failure mechanism of Superjunction MOSFET (SJ-MOS) in H3TRB-HVDC test was studied. By the comparison tests of SJ-MOS with different bias voltage, packaging materials and passivation layers, as well as the comparison tests between SJ-MOS and conventional power MOSFETs (C-MOS) with the same breakdown voltage class, it is found that both high electric field in the termination region, moisture and stress play important roles in the failure. Combined with simulation, a new failure model of H3TRB is proposed.

articleTitle: Investigation on the Influences of Affinity Variations of p-NiOx in Ga203 Fin-HJFETs at High Temperatures
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: In this work., the influences of affinity variations of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{p-NiO}_{\mathrm{x}}$</tex> in fin-based <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{p-NiO}_{\mathrm{x}}/\mathrm{n}-\text{Ga}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3}$</tex> heterojunction field-effect transistors (Fin-HJFETs) at high temperatures are investigated in details. An temperature dependent affinity model of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{p-NiO}_{\mathrm{x}}$</tex> is built by the mean of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{C}++\text{coding}$</tex> the temperature related partial derivative is 1 me V /K. Furthermore, a gate voltage model incorporating this affinity model is developed to investigate the reliability at high temperatures. Finally, it is revealed that the increase of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{p-NiO}_{\mathrm{x}}$</tex> affinity at high temperature almost not affect the transfer characteristics, but leads to the increase of gate leakage currents, resulting in reliability problems such as gate failure during short-circuit events.

articleTitle: New Insights using Avalanche Mode for On-wafer Evaluation of SiC Diodes Technology and Design Ruggedness
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: On-wafer measurements of 1200V rated 4H-SiC power diodes have been performed in near avalanche mode to investigate the stability and robustness of the devices. The method consists of biasing the SiC diodes at near-avalanche current or voltage levels for a variable period of time. The drifting of the static electrical parameters (leakage current, avalanche voltage, Schottky barrier height) is then studied. For two different SiC diode processing technologies, two drift behaviors of the blocking I-V curves were observed. Impact ionization, which is responsible for the avalanche phenomenon at high electric fields, has been localized and distinguished between the active region of the devices and the edge termination region, depending on the processing technology. Electroluminescence observations and numerical simulations were performed to confirm the interpretation of the electrical results. The robustness of the method was further supported.

articleTitle: Prompt Shift of On-State Resistance in LDMOS Devices: Causes, Recovery, and Reliability Implications
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: The present study reveals the occurrence of a sudden initial parameter shift, frequently referred as prompt shift, of the on-resistance due to operation points with high current flow during readouts. The shift is found to be partly recoverable, with recovery occurring on a logarithmic timescale. Additionally, the temperature behavior of the shift is observed to be similar to classical hot carrier injection (HCI), while its recovery is shown to diverge from classical bias temperature instability (BTI) recovery. These observations carry significant implications for the reproducibility of on-state resistance measurements and lifetime evaluation. Therefore, it is necessary to account for the immediate shift in on-state resistance measurements, which can be accurately predicted through a simple model proposed in this study, in order to conduct proper evaluation and get reliable and reproducible readouts.

articleTitle: Dynamic Charge Imbalance in Superjunction IGBTs: Design, Simulation, and Experimental Validation
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: To explore the potential of silicon Insulated Gate Bipolar Transistors (IGBTs), we conducted the design, simulation, and experimental validation of the 1.2 kV-class Superjunction (SJ) IGBTs for the first time. The SJ structure has been optimized to balance between bipolar conduction loss and ultra-fast switching capabilities, while withstanding a reverse breakdown voltage of 1.2 kV. Furthermore, our research has revealed the unique dynamic charge imbalance effect associated with SJ-IGBTs, which affects characteristics such as surge voltage <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(V_{\mathrm{s}\mathrm{u}\mathrm{r}\mathrm{g}\mathrm{e}})$</tex> and turn-off energy loss <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(E_{\mathrm{o}\mathrm{f}\mathrm{f}})$</tex> .

articleTitle: Improving the Short-Circuit Capability of RC-IEGT by Backside Double P-Ring Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: The reverse-conducting injection-enhanced gate transistor (RC-IEGT) is a device that has both p-type and n-type layers at the backside. It was found that the RC-IEGT has a weaker short-circuit capability compared to the conventional IEGT, which has a single p-type layer at the backside. We analyzed this issue using TCAD simulation and confirmed that the hole injection from the edge of the cell region is an important factor in suppressing the increase in the backside electric field. To improve the short-circuit capability without affecting the turn-off capability, we applied the backside double P-ring structure which injects the hole from the P-ring only at saturation current during short-circuit operation. As a result, the fabricated device showed an excellent short-circuit capability without any influence on other electrical characteristics, including the turn-off capability.

articleTitle: MOCVD Growth and Fabrication of Vertical P-i-N and Schottky Power Diodes Based on Ultra-wide Bandgap AlGaN Epitaxial Structures
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: We report epitaxial growth of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim$</tex>5-J.1m-thick high-AI-composition (HAC) AlGaN heterostructures on sapphire substrates by metal organic chemical vapor deposition (MOCVD). Cross-sectional and plan view transmission electron microscope (TEM) characterization was carried out to examine the dislocation behavior and density in the thick HAC AlGaN layer. Vertical AlGaN-based P-i-N and Schottky power diodes with state-of-the-art performance are fabricated and characterized, featuring measured breakdown voltages of 1032 V and 685 V, and calculated average breakdown electric fields of 3.44 MV /cm and 2.44 MV/cm, respectively. Both the P-i-N and Schottky diodes exhibit a much higher on/off ratio of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\sim 10^{8}$</tex>, compared to their ultra-wide bandgap counterparts of AIN based vertical diodes. The AlGaN P-i-N diodes exhibit stable on-state performance under 6–12 V /0.5-1000 s stress test, while a slight shift in the turn-on voltage is observed from the AlGaN-based Schottky diodes under 8 V/0.5-1000 s stress.

articleTitle: Demonstration of Split Double Gate $\text{CSTBT}^{\text{TM}}$ for Switching Loss Reduction
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: IGBTs have been improved by various innovations such as <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{CSTBT}^{\text{TM}}$</tex> [1]. The device performance has been approaching the physical limit. Recently, the focus has shifted towards the multi-gate driving as a means to overcome the limitation of switching loss reduction r2-81.

articleTitle: Impact of Diode Technology on the Switching Performance of 3.3 kV SiC MOSFETs
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: In this paper, the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3^{\text{rd}}$</tex> quadrant switching performance of 3.3 kV SiC MOSFETs with different diode configurations is compared. Switching energy measurements have been performed with a 2 kV DC link at different junction temperatures (from 25 to 150°C) and different switching rates up to 1.2 A/ns and 50 V/ns. The diode configurations include (i) body diode (BD), (ii) series connected 1.7 kV SiC Schottky Barrier Diode (SBD) with no BD conduction, (iii) series connected 1.7 kV SiC SBD in parallel with the body diode, (iv) 3.3 kV SiC SBD with no BD conduction, (v) 3.3 kV SiC SBD in parallel with the body diode, (vi) 3.3 kV SiC Merged PiN Schottky diodes (MPS) with no BD conduction, (vii) MPS diodes in parallel with the body diode and (viii) BD with synchronous rectification. The 3.3 kV SBD and 1.7 kV SBDs with no BD conduction demonstrate the best switching performance. The results also show that reverse recovery charge from the body diode contributes to additional losses when using two series 1.7 kV SBDs in parallel with the body diode due to high voltage drop across the SBDs. This paper also shows that using synchronous rectification significantly improves the switching performance of the BD when a dead-time of 240 ns is implemented between the high and low side transistors.

articleTitle: Normally-Off Schottky-Gate p-GaN HEMTs with Enhanced Irradiation Hardness
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: In this work, the p-type GaN layer (p-GaN) of the E-mode Schottky-gate GaN high electron mobility transistor (GaN HEMT) is patterned into designated segments, where one part of the p-GaN is buried with ohmic contact metal and connected to the source, while the other part serves as a real gate. This partitioned design of p-GaN can enable certain control of the channel by the source, and the gate is still functional. The threshold voltage (V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">TH</inf>) and ON-resistance <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(R_{\text{on}})$</tex> of the resulting device are 3.64 V and 0.22 Ω respectively, as compared to the traditional structure device (3.37 V, 0.19 Ω). Furthermore, the proposed device exhibits decent gate breakdown capability and long-term reliability, revealing the functionality of this specific structure design. By carrying out ultraviolet (UV) pulse laser-induced single-event effect (SEE) irradiation experiments, the breakdown capability of the device under single-event burnout (SEB) conditions is significantly enhanced, which is attributed to the effective dissipation of radiation-induced holes by the constructed buried ohmic structure.

articleTitle: Experiments of A Novel 3-D Charge Balanced Self-Shielding Isolation Technology for High-Voltage Integrated Circuits
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: A novel 3-dimensional charge-balanced self-shielding isolation (3-D CSI) technology is proposed and experimentally demonstrated in this paper based on a 0.35 μm bipolar-CMOS-DMOS (BCD) process platform. The 3-D CSI structure is realized by forming internal N-type islands in highly doped P-wells and introducing two deep N-well (DN) regions in the bulk of the device, in which ionized negative charges in the P-well, P-bury, and P-sub regions achieve 3-D charge balance with ionized positive charges in the surrounding DN, N-well, and internal N-well islands regions. The new technology widens the safe operating area (SOA) of the level-shifting Laterally Diffused MOSFET (LDMOS) while increasing the on-state current. In experiments, the breakdown voltage <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V$</tex><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">B</inf> of the level-shifting LDMOS using 3-D CSI technology was increased from 656 V of the conventional structure to 867 V with a leakage current of just 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">−11</sup> A. The 3-D CSI technology has passed 1000 hours of high-temperature reverse bias (HTRB) test and realized the commercial application.

articleTitle: A Novel E-Mode GaN p-MISFET with Hole Compensation Effect Achieving High Drain Current and Ultra-Low Subthreshold Slope
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: In this work, a novel enhancement-mode GaN p-MISFET featuring a Buried Back Gate (BBG) is proposed to achieve high drain current density and ultra-low subthreshold slope. With the delicately designed 2DEG back-gate channel on the p-GaN/AIN/AIGaN/AIN/GaN heterostructure platform, both of the p-channel current capability and the gate-to-channel control can be effectively enhanced. Compared to conventional GaN p-MISFETs, the BBG p-MISFET exhibits a significant increase in drain current density from −2.1 to −9.1 rnA/mm and a reduction in subthreshold slope from 148 to −60 mV/dec. The back-gate effect and hole compensation mechanism of the BBG p-MISFET have been thoroughly elucidated through TCAD simulation. Furthermore, mixed-mode simulations were conducted to validate the performance improvement of the basic inverter with the BBG p-MISFET based on monolithic integration, showcasing superior voltage conversion characteristics and dynamic switching behavior. The results suggest the potential applications of the proposed BBG p-MISFET in GaN-on-Si single-chip integrated complementary logic for high frequency and high efficiency GaN ICs.

articleTitle: 600 V 4H-SiC Lateral Bi-Directional JBS Diode Integrated MOSFET (L-BiD-JBSFET)
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: This paper presents the successful demonstration of a 600 V 4H-SiC lateral bi-directional JBS diode integrated MOSFET (L-BiD-JBSFET). The unit cell of the L-BiD-JBSFET is constructed by connecting two SiC lateral JBSFET unit cells back-to-back with a common-drain configuration. To explore the electrical characteristics of the SiC L-BiD-JBSFET, we begin by implementing and characterizing SiC lateral JBS diodes, SiC lateral MOSFETs, and SiC lateral JBSFET devices. Building on these findings, the unique features of SiC L-BiD-JBSFET are investigated, supported by simulation data. The fabricated L-BiD-JBSFET exhibits symmetric conduction and blocking characteristics, with improved conduction behavior attributed to Schottky embedding.

articleTitle: Bi-Directional Operation and Active Err Reduction of 2nd Generation Back-Gate-Controlled IGBTs (BC-IGBTs)
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: We demonstrated bi-directional operation and active reduction of reverse recovery loss (Err) in reverse conduction mode to realize freewheel diode (FWD) less switching of Back-gate-Controlled IGBT (BC-IGBT). Compared to conventional RC-IGBT, bi-directional BC-IGBT has advantages in terms of active Eoff, Err reduction, snapback free, and area efficiency. 2nd generation BC-IGBT was designed with the additional Deep P-layer (DP), which is able to reduce parasitic bipolar gain above the n-source region. DP can improve the Eoff-Vcesat tradeoff in the forward mode and also prevent latch-up failure in the reverse mode. Reverse recovery current can be dynamically suppressed by applying a front-side gate pulse just before the end of reverse conducting period. These results demonstrate that the BC-IGBT can achieve a freewheel diode (FWD)-less inverter and realize truly ideal bi-directional IGBTs.

articleTitle: Improved β-Ga2O3 Schottky Barrier Diodes Featuring p-NiO Gradual Junction Termination Extension within Mesa Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: In this work, we designed and fabricated high performance <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta-\text{Ga}_{2}\mathrm{o}_{3}$</tex> Schottky barrier diodes (SBDs) with composite termination that combines mesa and gradual junction termination extension (MJTE). The mesa avoids the peak electric field (E-field) at the anode periphery, while the design of gradual multilayer NiO effectively modulates the gradient of E-field distribution. Systematic TCAD simulations were conducted to study the relationship between E-field distribution with NiO thickness, mesa depth, and JTE length. Combined with the optimized parameters, the breakdown voltage of the device increased from 738 V to 2116 V, resulting in a seven-fold improvement in power figure-of-merit (PFOM) (from 81.05 MW/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> to 608.35 MW/cm2). This work provides a practical and effective solution for enhancing the performance of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta-\text{Ga}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3}$</tex> SBDs.

articleTitle: Experimental Demonstration of the Double-Trench, Buried-P JTE Edge Termination with Short Edge Width and High dV/dt Capability for 1200 V-class SiC Devices
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: A double trench, buried-P junction termination extension (DTBP-JTE) edge termination structure for 1200 V-class SiC devices is experimentally demonstrated. The proposed structure features a short JTE followed by two floating buried-P layers at the bottom of the double trenches. Process module of JTE and buried-P patterning has been developed and optimized to implement both the JTE and floating buried-P layers underneath the trenches simultaneously. Sidewall spacer of hard mask is adopted to eliminate thin P-layers at the trench sidewall, and thus ensure that the buried-P layers keep floating. Experimental results show that the fabricated DTBP-JTE edge termination achieves a BV of 1416 V with an edge width of only 19 μm. By comparison, the conventional guard-ring structure has a BV of 1358 V with an edge width of 103um. The DTBP-JTE achieves higher BV with a five times shorter edge width. Furthermore, the DTBP-JTE can pass the high dV/dt test under the condition of 88 V/ns with a bus voltage of 1200 V. Therefore, the DTBP-JTE achieves a better tradeoff between breakdown voltage and edge width without sacrificing the high dV/dt capability.

articleTitle: Improving the Surge Current Capability of SiC MOSFETs Under Positive Gate Bias
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: In SiC MOSFETs, the degradation of surge current capability when applying positive gate voltage has become a problem. To suppress the degradation of surge current capability, we conducted TCAD simulation to accurately understand the bipolar operation and heat generation inside the device during surge operation. Based on the results, we experimentally studied the improvement of device design and development of protection circuits. In device design, we showed that appropriate design of current spread resistance can improve surge current capability while minimizing the increase in on-resistance. We also studied protection circuits for surge operation by gate control and provided new guidelines for appropriate switching current and switching delay time.

articleTitle: Impact of Reverse Current Spreading on Diode Conduction Reliability Of SBD-Embedded SiC MOSFET with Deep P-Shield Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: The device structure of SBD-embedded MOSFET was investigated and the complicated tradeoff relationship of on-state resistance, short-circuit ruggedness, and diode conduction capability was improved. TCAD analysis indicated that bipolar conduction in body diode of MOSFET with deep p-shield can be suppressed by developing current spreading layer structure. The fabricated devices demonstrated adequate ruggedness in short-circuit operation and unipolar conduction capability in diode operation while obtaining low on-state resistance. The reduction in leakage by the developed structure enabled drift layer tuning and finally low on-resistance of 2.0 mΩ-cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>was demonstrated.

articleTitle: Evidence of Dynamic Input Capacitance of SiC Power MOSFETs
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: This paper presents an evidence of dynamic input capacitance <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C_{\text{gg}}$</tex> of SiC power MOSFETs. Based on the performed ramp-rate capacitance-voltage (C-V) measurements and circuit simulations, the dynamic <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C_{\text{gg}}$</tex> behavior is explained by the distributed internal gate resistance defined by the on-chip gate layout network and the time-constant of charge trapping due to the present defects at the SiC-oxide interface. The ramp-rate-based <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C_{\text{gg}}-V_{\text{gs}}$</tex> measurements with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{\text{gs}}$</tex> -ramp time of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$25\ \mu \mathrm{s}$</tex> are compared with the standard <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C_{\text{gg}}-V_{\text{gs}}$</tex> impedance analyzer (IA) measurements for a Si super-junction power MOSFET and two different SiC power MOSFETs. The differences between the ramp-rate- and the IA-based <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C_{\text{gg}}-V_{\text{gs}}$</tex> measured curves are more significant for the two SiC power MOSFETs compared to the Si power MOSFET. This is attributed to SiC-oxide interface states and their time constant. The presented ramp-rate <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$C_{\text{gg}}- V_{\text{gs}}$</tex> measurement method should more accurately capture the actual C-V behavior during fast switching events.

articleTitle: Trade-Off Between TID and SEGR Effects Based on High-Voltage Radiation-Hardened Gate Oxide
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: High-voltage (HV) MOSFET is more sensitive to the total ionizing dose (TID) effect due to the thick gate oxide that is used to keep from single-event gate rupture (SEGR) effect. The radiation-hardened gate oxide (RH-GOX) process makes a good tradeoff between TID effect and SEGR failure. Based on the heavily doped region and deep trench isolation technique, the MOSFET devices is designed by the interdigitated structure instead of enclosed-gate layout. The experimental results indicate that radiation-induced threshold voltage shifts <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\Delta V_{\text{th}})$</tex> have a strong dependence on bias conditions during radiation. In both the NMOS and PMOS transistors, radiation-induced threshold voltage shifts are proportional to power exponent of gate oxide thickness <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(T_{\text{ox}})$</tex>, and the coefficient factor is 1.12. With <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$T_{\text{ox}}=120$</tex> nm, the proposed circuit is not susceptible to SEGR failure with a linear energy transfer (LET) value of 82.7 Mev-cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>/mg.

articleTitle: 2kV Low Leakage Vertical NiO/β-Ga2O3 Hetero-Junction Diode and its Thermal/Electrical Stability
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: This work demonstrates a vertical <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{NiO}/\beta-\text{Ga}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3}$</tex> Heterojunction Diode (HJD) with a deep trench termination. The 7μm deep trench is etched using a self-aligned technique to reduce electric field at the anode edge. Additionally, a combined <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{SiO}_{2}/\text{PI}/\text{Si}\mathrm{O}_{2}$</tex> dielectric structure is used to fill the trench and an additional field plate is also used to reduce the electric field in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Ga}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3}$</tex>. TCAD simulations demonstrate a significant reduction in the electric field at the anode edge. The Mesa-HJD is fabricated along with the DT-HJD. The specific on resistance of them are both <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$2.4\mathrm{m}\Omega\cdot \text{cm}^{2}$</tex>. The fabricated DT-HJD shows a high breakdown voltage of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$> 2\text{kV}$</tex> with a doping concentration of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-3\times 10^{16}\text{cm}^{-3}$</tex>. Consequently, a high-Power Figure of Merit (PFOM) of 1. <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$75\text{GW}/\text{cm}^{2}$</tex> is hence achieved. Moreover, a remarkably low leakage current of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$10^{-5}\mathrm{A}/\text{cm}^{2}$</tex> at 1700 reverse bias is also achieved, which is among the lowest in multi-kilovolts <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Ga}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3}$</tex> HJDs. The results demonstrate the promising potential of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Ga}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3}$</tex> HJD for power electronics applications.

articleTitle: Closed-Loop Gate-Sensing Active Driver IC with Adaptive Delay Compensation Technique for Silicon Carbide Power MOSFETs
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: To permit an optimal tradeoff between current overshoot and switching losses (E<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">Loss</inf>) during the switching on of Silicon Carbide power MOSFETs (SiC), an active gate driver (AGD) IC is proposed in this paper. This AGD IC incorporates a gate-sensing technique without the requirement of external sensing components and adjusts the driving capability during turn-on, thereby suppressing current overshoot, oscillation, and electromagnetic interference (EMI) issues. Additionally, the proposed driver IC compensates for circuit propagation delay to enhance effectiveness in suppressing current-induced EMI. The proposed AGD is validated by the 0.18 μm HV BCD process. It achieves a remarkable 40.5% reduction in switching loss compared to the conventional gate driver (CGD) under similar current overshoot conditions. These results underscore the significant advancements the AGD offers in enhancing the efficiency and reliability of SiC-based power management systems.

articleTitle: Experiments of A Novel 600V SOI-LIGBT with Parallelly Discrete Cells for Amperage-Class Current Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: In this paper, a novel 600 V silicon-on-insulator lateral insulated-gate bipolar transistor with parallelly discrete cells (P-cell LIGBT) for amperage-class current integration is reported, which has a large current capability and a wide safe operating area (SOA). The amperage-class current integration is achieved in the P-cell LIGBT through 8 parallelly discrete cells. By using a parallel structure, the novel P-cell LIGBT completely avoids the high electric field from the curvature effect at the cathode-center termination of the conventional structure. In addition, a series of stepped shield rings are introduced between the high-voltage interconnect (HVI) and the drift region to shield the strong field modulation of the HVI on the device and also can be used as a field plate structure to optimize the surface electric field. The fabricated P-cell LIGBT realized a high breakdown voltage V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">B</inf> of 651 V, and current capability up to 5 ampere level in the on state.

articleTitle: Gate Oxide Failure Mechanisms of SiC MOSFET Related to Electro-Thermomechanical Stress Under HTRB and HTGB Test
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: Reliability issues with the gate oxide remain a significant obstacle to the widespread application of SiC MOSFET devices. This work reveals the gate oxide failure of SiC MOSFETs not only related to gate oxide defects and high electric fields but also to thermomechanical stress. During the High Temperature Reverse Bias (HTRB) and High Temperature Gate Bias (HTGB) tests, the unique structure of the MOSFET device cells and gate pad transition region experiences concentrated thermomechanical stress at high temperatures, as the mismatch in coefficient of thermal expansion (CTE) between SiC/SiO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> and Poly-Si/SiC leads to more pronounced stress concentration, resulting in gate oxide failure in these areas. In the HTGB test, the high electric field in the gate oxide accelerates the failure process in conjunction with thermomechanical stress. By optimizing the layout pattern and process, the mechanical stress at the failure point was reduced by 56.5%, and the optimized devices passed 1000 hours of HTRB and HTGB testing.

articleTitle: Comprehensive Study of Human-Body-Model Electrostatic Discharge on p-GaN Gate Power HEMT with AlGaN Barrier Spacers
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: This paper presents an investigation into the improvement of gate ESD robustness in Schottky gate p-GaN high electron mobility transistors (HEMTs) through the utilization of gate epitaxial engineering. The proposed device with optimized AlGaN spacers features comparable DC on-state and off-state performances, while the forward gate-to-source (G-S) and gate-to-source (G-D) of the Human-Body-Model (HBM) Electrostatic Discharge (ESD) capability is significantly boosted from 300 V to 3.5 kV, meeting the JEDEC JS-001-2023 Class 2 standard compared to that without an AlGaN spacer structure. In addition, the influences of HBM stress on the device stability and reliability has been evaluated. The proposed device shows negligible shifts in time-dependent gate breakdown (TDGB) and dynamic performance after being subjected to G-S HBM ESD testing under the Class 2 standard. At a high HBM voltage of 3.5 kV, the proposed mechanism explains the accumulation of holes at the p-GaN/AlGaN and AlGaN/GaN interfaces, which lowers barriers and improves electron conduction capabilities and uniformity under the gate, thereby alleviating current crowding. The reverse G-S HBM ESD capability strongly depends on the reverse blocking voltage of the gate-to-source terminal. As a result, this study has proposed a potential solution without gate ESD protection circuits, enabling the achievement of HBM ESD capability within specification.

articleTitle: Explorative Study of a Novel Desaturation IGBT with Transconductance Modulation
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: Based on the Micro Pattern Trench (MPT) technology, we reduced the distance, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d$</tex>, between the main gate (G1) and the desaturation gate (G2) within an IGBT cell. We observed that if <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d$</tex> is longer, the G2 voltage, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{\mathrm{G}2}$</tex>, has almost no impact on the transfer characteristics as long as it stays below the threshold voltage. This behavior is consistent with earlier research. However, for very short <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$d$</tex> we found a modulation of the transconductance. Our study explains the effect of this modulation, shows how it can be used to improve turn-off desaturation, and how it impacts the IGBT's turn-on behavior through both TCAD simulation and demonstrator chips. A comparison with conventional single-gate IGBTs and SiC MOSFETs has revealed the high potential of desaturation IGBTs. This is also underlined by RB-SOA test results.

articleTitle: First Demonstration of All-SiC Half-Bridge Gate Driver with High-Side Floating Substrate Region
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: This paper proposes a 200V all-SiC integration process platform integrating low-voltage (LV) and high-voltage (HV) devices, such as LV NMOS, LV PMOS, resistor, capacitor, HV LDMOS, and HV Diode. Based on these devices, a 200V half-bridge driver composed of a low-side driver and a high-side driver was designed and fabricated. Then, the half-bridge driver was packaged and measured. The measurement results shows that the proposed half-bridge driver can operate normally at 25°C and 200°C.

articleTitle: Demonstration of the p-GaN Gate HEMT with Crystalline GaOx/GaOxN1-xPassivation
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: We investigate GaN HEMT devices with a crystalline <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{GaO}_{\mathrm{x}}/\text{GaO}_{\mathrm{x}}\mathrm{N}_{1-\mathrm{x}}$</tex> passivation layer. The p-GaN layer, subjected to oxygen plasma treatment (OPT) and post-annealing process (PA), transforms into a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{GaO}_{\mathrm{x}}/\text{GaO}_{\mathrm{x}}\mathrm{N}_{1-\mathrm{x}}$</tex> layer, leading to the recovery of the depleted two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG) underneath. The p-GaN HEMTs with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{GaO}_{\mathrm{x}}/\text{GaO}_{\mathrm{x}}\mathrm{N}_{1-\mathrm{x}}$</tex> passivation exhibit satisfactory characteristics at a PA temperature of 450°C with an <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I_{\text{ON}}/I_{\text{OFF}}$</tex> ratio <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$> 10^{8}$</tex>. Additionally, the OFF-state breakdown voltage reached 1018 V for a gate-to-drain separation of 15 μm. The results indicate the merits of employing <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{GaO}_{\mathrm{x}}/\text{GaO}_{\mathrm{x}}\mathrm{N}_{1- \mathrm{x}}$</tex> passivation to realize the p-GaN HEMT.

articleTitle: A Novel MOS Controllable Stored-Carrier Diode (MOSD) for An Innovative Silicon Power Device (i-Si)
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: A novel MOS controllable stored-carrier diode (MOSD) is proposed, that can break through V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">F</inf> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{E}_{\text{rr}}$</tex> tradeoff for conventional pn-diode. The MOSD, which consists of a low-injection <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{p}^{-}$</tex> layer, injection-promoting <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{p}^{+}$</tex> layer, Electron Barrier layer, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{n}^{+}$</tex> layer, and surrounding MOS gate, enables control of stored-carrier density using gate bias during diode conduction, and a high-breakdown voltage independent of gate bias during blocking. A 6.5 kV MOSD shows extremely lower V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">F</inf> <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(-1.0\mathrm{V})$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{E}_{\text{rr}}+\mathrm{E}_{\text{on}}$</tex> (−43%) than the ultra-soft & fast recovery pn-diode (U-SFD). An innovative silicon power device (i-Si) consisting of the proposed MOSD and dual side-gate high-conductivity IG:BT through time and space control of stored-carrier (TASC-HiGT), which are made entirely from silicon, demonstrated −40% inverter loss of pn-diode and IGBT, equivalent to SiC-DMOSFET.

articleTitle: Refining Accuracy: A Quasi-Floating Channel SPICE Model for Third-Quadrant SiC MOSFET Analysis in Both Planar and Trench Structures
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: This paper presents an improved SPICE model for SiC MOSFETs. We introduce a model dividing SiC MOSFET operation into a PN diode and a quasi-floating channel (QFC) model, specifically addressing the third quadrant operational mode. This approach significantly reduces root mean square error in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I_{D}-V_{D}$</tex> characteristics compared to conventional models, as demonstrated by experimental data from dynamic switching experiments and comparative analysis. The proposed model exhibits a marked improvement in replicating real-world operational dynamics of SiC MOSFETs, especially in dynamic scenarios. With a maximum 95% reduction in RMSE and enhanced computational efficiency, the model is established as a valuable tool for advanced SiC MOSFET simulation and analysis, impacting the efficiency, performance, and reliability of power electronic systems.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Trap Parameters of RC-IGBT After Repetitive Avalanche Stress by DLTS Simulation
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: This study examines traps responsible for deterioration in power semiconductors following exposure to avalanche stress. By utilizing deep-level transient spectroscopy (DLTS) analysis and TCAD simulation, we aim to explore the effects of repetitive avalanche stress (equivalent to 1/10 of the destructive level) on the reverse conducting IGBT (RC-IGBT) devices. Peaks corresponding to donor and acceptor-type carrier traps are observed in the DLTS signal, indicating changes in carrier density, feedback capacitance, and turn-off characteristics. This approach allows for the evaluation of traps, assessment of their distribution, and simulation of the degradation of electrical characteristics caused by avalanche stress.

articleTitle: An Integrated Low-Power Enhanced Pull-Up GaN Driver Using SenseHEMT for Reliable and Fast Short-Circuit Protection
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: This article proposed an integrated GaN driver with a low-power enhanced pull-up (LPEP) technique to achieve the decoupling between the charging path and the leakage path of the inverter in the driver. Considering the poor short-circuit tolerance of GaN power HEMTs, a low-loss fast short-circuit detection (FSCD) technique using senseHEMT is proposed for reliable and fast short-circuit protection. Experimental results show that the leakage current of the single-stage inverter is 28μA and the rise time of the gate voltage <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{\mathrm{G}}$</tex> of powerHEMT is 0.71ns. The measured minimum short-circuit response time is 37ns.

articleTitle: A Monolithic Bi-Directional GaN/SiC Hybrid Field-Effect Transistor
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: Power electronics systems such as matrix converters require devices that are capable of blocking high voltage and conducting current in both forward and reverse directions. In this work, we present a monolithic bi-directional GaN/SiC hybrid field-effect transistor (BD-HyFET). The device combines the merits of SiC junction field-effect transistor (JFET) structure and p-GaN gated 2-dimensional-electron-gas (2DEG) channel, enabling the inclusion of a high mobility channel and area-efficient vertical voltage blocking structure. The fabricated devices exhibit bi-directional behavior at both OFF-state and ON-state, with almost symmetrical characteristics in the 1<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">st</sup> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$3^{\text{rd}}$</tex> I-<tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V$</tex> quadrants. Non-destructive off-state breakdown characteristics with breakdown voltages over 600 V were obtained in both forward and reverse directions. The four-quadrant switching characteristics of the GaN/SiC BD-HyFET were verified. In addition, the characteristics of the BD-HyFET as an AC power chopper were successfully demonstrated.

articleTitle: Determination of the Junction Temperature Under Load Current in GaN Power Devices with Schottky Gate Leakage Current as TSEP
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: The junction temperature of power semiconductor devices is an important parameter for power system design and reliability determination. In lateral GaN power devices, no pn-junction is present in the load current path and the commonly used <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V$</tex><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">CE</inf> (T) method cannot be applied. For Schottky p-GaN devices, the forward gate leakage current of the Schottky barrier can be used as temperature sensitive electrical parameter (TSEP). By monitoring the gate current at constant gate voltage, a load current independent temperature sensing is applicable. In this paper the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I$</tex><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">G</inf> (T)-method is used for thermal impedance measurement.

articleTitle: Single-Event Effects in SiC Power MOSFET Induced by Pulsed-Laser Two Photon Absorption
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: Single-event effect (SEE) especially single-event burnout (SEB) threshold voltage is investigated in SiC MOSFETs in both experiment and simulation. Pulsed-laser two photon absorption (TPA) technique is used in experiments with three depths of focus (DOF) (Of.lm, 3f.lm, 6f.lm) and three energies (E) (20nJ, 35nJ, 50nJ). Experimental data for 1.2kV MOSFET shows that the SEB threshold voltage is 450V at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$DOF=3\mu \mathrm{m}$</tex>, which is lowest among all three depths of focus. SEB threshold voltage is proved to have a positive correlation with device voltage rating and a negative correlation with laser energy. Devices with three voltage ratings (1.2kV, 1.7kV, 3.3kV) are studied and two different single-event effects were observed with increasing drain-source voltage at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$DOF=3\mu\mathrm{m}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E$</tex> =50nJ. TCAD simulation demonstrates that high electrical field and high avalanche current localized near SiC N-/N+ interface lead to extreme local power dissipation and rapid lattice temperature rising (> 1500K), and cause the SEB in SiC MOSFETs.

articleTitle: Investigation of Trap States and Reverse Leakage in Fully-Vertical GaN Schottky Barrier Diodes with Laser Lift-Off Substrate
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: Lase lift-off (LLO) substrate technology is a promising solution for realizing fully vertical GaN devices based on foreign substrates. By performing deep-level transient spectroscopy (DLTS) experiments and temperature-dependent leakage current characterizations, this work investigates the trap states and leakage mechanisms of fully-vertical GaN Schottky barrier diodes (SBDs) based on LLO substrate, laser annealing and N-implantation termination. By fitting the DLTS spectral signal, the energy levels of the two electron trap states are determined to be <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E_{C}$</tex> - 0.6 e V and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$E_{C}$</tex> - 0.21 eV respectively, which should originate from the intrinsic traps in GaN epitaxy rather than being introduced by the LLO process. Furthermore, the leakage currents of the device are found to be dominated by Poole-Frenkel emission (PFE, < 35 V), variable range hopping (VRH, 35 ~ 100 V) and trap-assisted tunneling (TAT, > 100 V), respectively, as the bias voltage increases. These results provide important new insights into the implementation of laser lift-off technology in GaN-based power devices.

articleTitle: A Quad-Slope Smart Gate Driver with Mixed-Signal Auto-Timing Technique for Power Devices Segment Control
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: This study categorizes the power devices' turn-on process into four stages with distinct gate rise slopes to enable segmented functionality. An innovative mixed-signal auto-timing (MSAT) technique is introduced to achieve segmented control with a width modulation range and high control precision. Furthermore, to enhance flexibility in common-mode noise control, the closed-loop enhanced control (CLEC) technique is proposed to adaptively regulate common-mode noise within a predefined range. The quad-slope smart gate driver proposed in this study is implemented in a 180-nm 40 V BCD process. The implementation results demonstrate its effectiveness in achieving segmented control under different target dv/dt values.

articleTitle: A Novel Degradation Mechanism of SiC Power Devices Under Electro-Chemical Stress
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: The goal of this work is to assess the failure mechanisms of SiC MOSFETs after long term H3TRB testing. For that purpose, an H3TRB test was performed on power modules with SiC MOSFET chips until all devices reached their parametric end-of-life. The results of the failure analysis showed that all tested chips exhibit vertical cracks through the chip near the edges. A chemical analysis suggests that the cracks originate from oxidation near the edges of the chip. The resulting volume increase, caused by the oxidation process, lead to mechanical stress and eventually the formation of vertical cracks of the SiC crystal in the respective area. Since this effect is not known for silicon devices, this could be a novel degradation mechanism, possibly unique to SiC. Even though the characteristic lifetime of the failure distribution is much longer that typical qualification criteria the acceleration factor with respect to field conditions is yet unknown and thus, should be further investigated.

articleTitle: A 200V High-Speed Level Shifter for Monolithic GaN IC with Enhanced $\mathrm{d}V_\mathrm{S}/\text{dt}$ Noise Immunity and Negative $V_\mathrm{S}$ Tolerance
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: The monolithic GaN half-bridge power IC minimizes parasitics and fully unleashes the high-speed capabilities of GaN devices. However, due to the unique characteristics of GaN devices and processes, reliability issues faced by level shifters in GaN half-bridge ICs are more severe. This study presents a GaN-based 200V high-speed level shifter with enhanced <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{d}V\mathrm{s}/\mathrm{d}t$</tex> noise immunity and negative <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_\mathrm{S}$</tex> tolerance. The new structure, composed of common-gate differential pairs, achieves a better trade-off between <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathrm{d}V\mathrm{s}/\mathrm{d}t$</tex> noise immunity capability and propagation delay. Additionally, the negative <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V_{\mathrm{S}}$</tex> tolerance of the level shifter has been strengthened by a concise circuit to accommodate the high reverse conduction voltage drop of GaN devices. Measured results verify the characteristics of the proposed circuit, which was fabricated using a 1μm GaN-on-Silicon process.

articleTitle: On-Line Digital Fine Monitoring of SiC MOSFET Gate-Oxide Health: A Dual-Channel Gate Driving Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: SiC power MOSFETs, compared to their Si counterparts, still lack maturity, hindering their adoption in aeronautical applications. Consequently, there is a growing need for the development of smart gate drivers with built-in functions like health monitoring. Reducing failures and downtime in power converters relies on an early detection of component ageing. However, assessing reliably the health condition of power transistors in PWM operation remains a challenge. In this perspective, a non-invasive strategy is proposed. This approach aims to determine precisely and accurately the health state of the gate oxide of a SiC power MOSFET. It uses a dual-channel gate driver to trigger a slow turn-on event and clean switching measurement within a PWM frame. This method involves an online tracking of oxide ageing, or charge-trapping indicators present in the gate signal waveform.

articleTitle: Kilovolt, Low-Barrier Ga2O3 JBS diode with Ultra-Low Forward Voltage
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: Gallium oxide <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\text{Ga}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3})$</tex> has attracted extensive attention for next-generation power devices. However, the reported <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Ga}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3}$</tex> rectifiers typically exhibit high turn-on voltage (VON) and forward voltage drop <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(V_{\mathrm{F}})$</tex>, leading to increased conduction losses. Conventional power SBDs are limited by a tradeoff between <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$V$</tex><inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">F</inf> and leakage current <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(I_{\mathrm{R}})$</tex>, which may pose a critical challenge for ultra-wide bandgap (UWBG) SBDs due to the high junction electric field (and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$I_{\mathrm{R}}$</tex>). This work demonstrates the first <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Ga}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3}$</tex> JBS diode with a low-barrier Schottky contact. Deploying the TiN contact, an ultra-low VON of 0.52 V and V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">F</inf> of 1 V [at forward current <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(I_{\mathrm{F}})$</tex> of 150 A/cm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>], along with a high breakdown voltage (BV) over 1 kV, are demonstrated in <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Ga}2\mathrm{O}_{3}$</tex> JBS diodes. Such V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">F</inf> is lower than the usual V<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">F</inf> of commercial 650V-rated SiC JBS diodes (1.3~1.8 V), indicating the promise of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Ga}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3}$</tex> JBS diode for power electronics applications. In addition to device innovation, this work also presents the first comparison of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Ga}_{2}\mathrm{O}_{3}$</tex> JBS diodes formed along [100] and [010] orientations, which reveals the strong impact of the orientation anisotropy of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Ga}2\mathrm{O}_{3}$</tex> on the JBS device performance.

articleTitle: Reducing Reverse Recovery Charge in Trench Power MOSFETs Using Platinum Traps Introduced by Implantation and PVD
publicationTitle: 2024 36th International Symposium on Power Semiconductor Devices and ICs (ISPSD)
abstract: Trench power MOSFETs are widely used across consumer, automotive and industrial market segments for many applications. During switching, the reverse recovery charge (Qrr) associated with the body diode of the MOSFET, gives rise to spiking, ringing and efficiency losses. In this study, minority carrier lifetime reduction/killing using Platinum (Pt) in trench power MOSFETs is demonstrated in terms of Qrr reduction. Further, reduced Qrr levels due to the presence of Pt traps, created by two different methods are compared, i) by ion implantation (Pt IMP) and ii) by physical vapor deposition (Pt PVD).
